floors.name: The Iron Tangle
floors.premise: All aboard! Floor four is every subway system on your planet, welded into one knot and set running. Trains, stations, and things that live on both. The stairwells don't open until six hours before collapse, so don't bother looking for a shortcut. Also, everyone on the leaderboard now has a bounty. Hunting season is open!

recap.title: All aboard
recap.text: They land on a red-line train already filling with Drek babies, and Carl finds the Protective Shell's best trick: cast on a straight run of track, it stays put while the train keeps moving, so it sweeps every car behind it clean. Donut's class must change now, and on six minutes' notice she becomes a Football Hooligan; Mordecai notices, and tells nobody, that she keeps any skill she levels even once. A court order lands on the AI's desk over the third floor, and its apology is a free personal space: beds, showers, a crafting studio and a training room. Mordecai has them on a schedule: two hours' sleep, buffs, an hour in the training room, a bench. Katia, whose constitution doubles on a moving train, goes through every door first. In the personal space Carl finds a folder he had missed, Messages from deceased Crawlers. Brandon held the line on the third floor so Imani and Elle could reach the stairs, and he asks Carl to tell Chris that he loved him. The Tangle is a maze of looping lines and transfer stations, every one numbered with a prime, and the NPCs who work it believe in wives and houses they have never had. Vernon the conductor dies under Donut's prize suitcase, which is full of burning ants. Then a fan box spins up the Prize Carousel, Mordecai throws a chair at its host and is suspended for seven days, and Carl passes over his father's old Harley to choose a thick book with an anarchy sign on the cover.

recap.title: The Cookbook
recap.text: The book is the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, and Carl is its twenty-fifth holder. Crawlers from other worlds and other seasons have carried it down and written in its margins: bomb recipes, notes on NPCs, a brother's grief, a philosopher's last essay. At the Desperado Club they hire two rock-monster bodyguards, Bomo and the Sledge, and meet Elle, a floating Frost Maiden now, and Imani, who tells them Chris picked a rock race, turned hard, and went off hunting. Donut dances on the Sledge's shoulders, is jumped by two crawlers, and kills one of them. A skull appears after her name, which she never wanted. Elle puts an icicle through the other and tells the room that anyone who comes for Donut comes for all of them. The club's assistant manager, a hand-sized sprite called Astrid, apologises in person and makes the bodyguards permanent. Carl spins the casino wheel on a hundred-thousand chip and wins a Scroll of Upgrade for his toe ring. He derails a train to get at its engineer, Gore-Gore, and learns two things about the Tangle: at station 435 the crews are wiped through a portal, and each punch of the gauntlet on a worshipper of Grull adds a point and a half towards summoning him. Carl stops at ten and a half by drop-kicking the mantaur onto the third rail. Sponsors arrive: the Valtay for Carl, Princess D'nadia for Donut, and Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire, the Maestro's little sister, for Katia. Donut takes the head off a war mage with Hole.

recap.title: Stealing the Nightmare Express
recap.text: Carl fist-bumps every crawler in the club and starts a chat network, so that what one of them learns, everyone learns. Then he steals a train. The Nightmare Express is a black steam engine towing forty cages of monsters. He stands in its tunnel, casts the shell as it arrives to wipe every car clean, misses the jump for the platform, is hit by the engine, and climbs in through the cab window to find two dead engineers and a boiler about to blow. Fire Brandy, a lesser demon who stokes the firebox and gives birth to her fuel, talks him through the valves. The train takes them to station 436, one past the end of the line, where every colour of train is thrown engineless into a burning pit a mile across. The souvenir conductor hats handed out on day one are keys out of it. Through a repair portal they reach a trainyard overrun by ghouls, where a grease gremlin called Widget tells them about the Escape Velocity line and a second after that the ghoul behind him tears his head off. Madison from human resources explains that the six Terminus stations are mimics, and that the six-armed Kravyad who guard the crews are paid in dwarves. Katia gives Carl a slip of paper she saw Donut hide under the track: a player-killer coupon with his name on it. At the club a drunk, one-handed Frank Q slips Carl a Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering as his revenge. That ring is why nothing could heal Yvette.

recap.title: Hekla
recap.text: On a beauty-pageant show filmed from a submarine, Carl refuses to read the script and steals the fridge shelves, the makeup table and the couch. Donut explains the coupons: she buried his under a track and threw Katia's in a bin. Frank Q is dead at the club bar, killed by Chris. Then Hekla arrives in the personal space with thirty of Brynhild's Daughters: a thousand crawlers are stranded at station 101, Li Jun's team among them, and a train is waiting at 60. Katia volunteers to be its plough, a ton and a quarter of scoop bolted to the front, because the Daughters came back for her and nobody ever has before. Carl does not trust Eva, the four-armed enforcer at Hekla's shoulder. In the middle of the ghoul horde, Donut's new goggles show Hekla putting invisible bolts into Katia's back, and the healer riding with them waiting for orders before she heals. The plan was to have Katia die, Carl lose his temper, Hekla put him down, and the Daughters inherit Donut and Mordecai. Donut puts a full-strength missile into Hekla's face. Eva mocks Katia in her own voice until Katia uses Rush, which she hates, and misses Eva by inches. Hekla hits the cab wall instead, and does not get up. Donut raises the corpse three times over and throws Eva out of the window. Katia now has a golden skull over her head and half a million gold on her own head, and an agent called Loita, from the party that runs Borant, lays claim to their account.

recap.title: Six hundred hats
recap.text: Six hundred crawlers are stranded at the pit with no hats, and station 75's yard holds ten rapid-response carts whose blades are portals: set them to the abyss to clear a line, or to a trainyard to rescue whoever is standing on it. Each cart wants two gnoll left hands to start. The only gnoll is Growler Gary, a bartender who cannot leave his bar and comes back to life every time he dies. Carl explains why, and Gary says yes. The recap plays it for laughs and shows none of the reason. The carts go out playing whatever the alarm trap picks, Physical by Olivia Newton John among them, and when Bautista's cart fails to arrive Carl rides the Mindaro line himself. On the way he accidentally sends a whole station mimic to trainyard E, and there are hats enough for everyone: six hundred crawlers step through the great portal to safety. A line of them lay their own hats at Donut's feet and bow. Carl sends the battered Vermillion engine down the tunnel full of dynamite and blocks the ghouls short of station 36. Stage-three DT monsters begin to burst into thousands of rice-sized Krakaren. Mordecai comes back from his seven days to find two new skulls on the team, Katia exploding in a shower of stored blood, and a ring he makes Carl take off with a smack to the head. Then he explains the map: from above, the lines make the Syndicate logo, and the pit is the centre of the galaxy.

recap.title: The Tangle eats itself
recap.text: At one day left the Iron Tangle announces its own destruction. The centres of the stations fall away and the Krakaren pour up into every room. At station 36 they pour straight into a portal cart Carl has hung nose-down over the hole on Imani's chain. The plan is to blow every ghoul generator in the system at once, and on the far side of the knot Prepotente, a talking goat with a patient taste for murder, and Miriam Dom are doing the same thing. Carl sends a province boss to the abyss that Prepotente was two hours from killing, and Donut is called delightful. Then a neighbourhood boss clamps a hand around Carl's foot and drags him through a portal into Trainyard E. The world freezes and the heavy metal starts: a Death Challenge. On one side a level-ninety Mimic Rex. On the other the war god Grull, summoned through the gauntlet and driven, the announcer says, by his sponsor: the Maestro, alive after all. Grull splits the mimic in half and steps on Carl, who survives it on Mordecai's Special Brew. Elle bounces icicles off the god's head, Katia turns herself into Carl and stands on a wrecked train giving him the finger, and Li Na brings a second vessel, arms and legs removed, to throw into the portal. The god goes with it. Fire Brandy and the conductor Tizquick ride the Nightmare Express into the pit to blow the generators, and the survivors live. On the stairs Carl writes in the Cookbook that twenty-four crawlers before him talked about burning this place down, and none of them did. I will break them all.

floors.previously: In the Over City: Donut became a Former Child Actor with Mordecai as her unwilling manager, and Carl became a Compensated Anarchist, which remains my favourite class name. They helped a circus elite get her banishment lifted, told an orc empire to overthrow itself on live television, and watched a pop star die in the trailer meant for them. They picked up Katia, a doppelganger ten levels behind. And at the end Carl shut a collapsing soul crystal inside a glass case and put the bomb in his pocket, where it still is. The house then refused to pay out eighty-three Celestial boxes. You're welcome.

steps.text: The floor is a railway, and nobody starts it on solid ground. Every party arrives aboard a train already moving through a tunnel, with ten days on the clock. The sign over each car door gives the line, the car number and the next stop, and every stop has a number. The shops and the inns are at the stations. There are 9,375 stairwells somewhere on the floor, and nobody has a map. Arriving earns a souvenir conductor's hat embroidered I rode the Iron Tangle. It is not magical.

Trains run one way only, climbing the numbers from station 11 to station 435, one every ten to fifteen minutes. Where lines cross there is a transfer station, with a saferoom, shops, and platforms the monsters do not come onto. The map on the platform says stairwells appear at stations 12, 24, 36, 48 and 72 on any coloured line. Every party starts somewhere above 80, and no train runs back down. There are 9,375 stairwells and ten days to find one.

Trains climb one way, from station 11 to station 435. Transfer stations, where lines cross, have saferooms and shops, and their platforms are safe. Stairwells appear at stations 12, 24, 36, 48 and 72 on any coloured line, and every party starts above 80. On this floor only, nobody goes down early: the stairwells open six hours before collapse and not a minute sooner. The leaderboard has filled, and each of its top ten carries a bounty. Kill one and the bounty arrives in a loot box; still be on the list when the floor ends and you keep ten percent of your own.

Trains climb one way, from station 11 to station 435, and the stairwells are at 12, 24, 36, 48 and 72 on every coloured line, sealed until six hours before collapse. Every line counts with the same numbers, so there are many stations 83. Every transfer station is a prime number. One whose number ends in a 1 has a Desperado Club; one ending in 9 has a Club Vanquisher. Each line runs hundreds of trains, and is said to have only one of the big named trains like the Nightmare Express. At every stop ending in a 5 or a 0 the monsters get off. Station 433 is the last transfer station and 434 is barren. At 435 the crews leave through a portal back to the depot, and each train is driven on through a gate just past it.

Trains climb one way, from 11 to 435, and the stairwells sit at 12, 24, 36, 48 and 72, sealed until six hours before collapse. The way back to the low numbers is through the end of the line. Past 435 every train is driven through a portal into the abyss at station 436, and the souvenir hat is a key: a crawler wearing it who rides to the end is carried through to a trainyard, though the car they rode in is not. An engineer's key takes the car through as well. The crews' own portal at 435 may also work, and so may a named line that stops at 436, if someone can drive it to the switching station.

The Iron Tangle has declared itself broken down and started its own self-destruct. No line is running. Emergency escape tunnels are opening throughout the system, with a warning about gravitational shifts inside them. The stairwell portals at stations 12, 24, 36, 48, 72 and 433 on every line are powering up. They open eighteen hours after the announcement and stay open for six, and then the self-destruct charges blow.

The crawlers arrive in the last car of a twenty-car Red Line train: a Moscow Metro car with Cyrillic graffiti, torn brown cushions and scorched plastic walls, the tunnel wall inches from the window. Zoomed all the way out, the map shows tubes everywhere, like a mess of noodles, and other trains shoot past at angles on the far side of the walls. The first car is a sealed block, and cars five, ten and fifteen are not passenger cars. The first stop is Sirin Station, number 81.

Station 83 is a transfer station. Its platform is long and concrete, with white tile walls, one bench and a faded yellow stripe at the edge, above a track channel five feet deep with an uncovered third rail. A short flight of stairs climbs to a small round room with a saferoom, a general store and a guild, and two more stairways lead down from it to the yellow line and the Nightmare Express. On the platform map the Red Line is one long red squiggle from 11 to 435.

Every line is its own shape on the map: the Red Line a squiggle, the yellow line an upside-down fishhook, and the Nightmare Express, on wider track from a platform twice as long, a figure eight of five stops with station 436 at its top. The same numbers repeat on every line, so the Nightmare passes two different stations 283 and two different 83s. A transfer station is a platform or three and a small round room of shops. An ordinary stop opens off its platform into caves: twisting tunnels, rooms where the monsters gather for the next train, and down a concrete hallway at the back, a warehouse behind barn doors. At station 131 the Desperado Club is a tiny dive bar with a neon sign.

The lines twist through the rock like noodles, each its own shape, every one counting with the same station numbers. Transfer stations are small rooms of shops over their platforms; ordinary stops open into caves where the monsters live. At the top of the Nightmare's figure eight is Abyss Station, 436: a bare platform and one steep iron stair that takes an hour to climb. At the top is a catwalk around a burning pit, almost perfectly round, at least a mile across and thousands of feet deep. Its walls are studded with hundreds, perhaps thousands, of glowing portals, and out of them the trains burst and fall. The bottom is a heap of wrecked cars with hundreds of fires on it. Through the portals lies a trainyard of engine cars behind a high fence, crowded with zombies.

The lines climb through the rock from 11 to 435, and the end of every one is the burning pit at 436, walled with portals. Behind those portals is a trainyard in a cavern: at least a mile from the portal to the fence, watchtowers at regular intervals, service bays under corrugated awnings, a baseball-field-sized turntable, and dozens of tracks converging through a pair of huge gates. Outside the gates of Trainyard E, Substation E burns. An employee line runs back from the yard with a service hatch at every station, and the low numbers are real. A stairwell station is a rock room the size of a warehouse with five sealed stairwells in a circle under shafts of light and ten exits down to platforms, one of them the Escape Velocity III. Station 59 has twenty-seven platforms. Station 60 is a single cobwebbed platform.

The Tangle has a plan after all. Seen from above, the named lines draw the logo of the Syndicate, a set of overlapping rings, and the abyss is the centre of the galaxy: the whole floor is a simplified map of it, the tracks the original worm paths. Each line is a noodle with track on the outside of it, and on the far side of the same noodle runs a second track, upside down, a station beneath every station with an empty chamber between the two. The six station mimics are so big because each one fills two stations at once. Around it all are the burning pit at 436, the trainyards behind their portals, and the stairwell rooms at 12, 24, 36, 48 and 72.

Monsters ride the trains, boarding at their own stations. Drek, demonic grey babies with too many teeth, travel in packs of at least fifty. In car fifteen are the Jikininki, ghouls of the Iron Tangle Rail System who work as its janitors. They leave you alone as long as you are not bleeding, not littering and not in their space. Somebody runs the stations, because there are inns and shops at them.

Monsters board at their own stations and ride a few stops; every fifth stop the train empties. Each train has a crew. An engineer is shut in the sealed first car. A dwarf conductor keeps a bar in car five, grapple porters keep racks of suitcases in car ten, and Jikininki janitors sweep the cars with brooms and try to eat the conductor. Vernon, the yellow line's conductor, remembers reaching 435 and then nothing until he stands on the platform at station 10, the yard, ready to start again. He is saving gold to go home to his wife. At the stations a mole man keeps the shop and a Bopca keeps the saferoom.

The monsters ride for a reason. At every stop ending in a 5 or a 0 they get off, line up by race and file down a tunnel to a door with a slot. Behind it is a Pooka, a fuzzy goblin of a neighbourhood boss that turns into a giant goat when attacked, who hands each one a vial of a race-specific sedative. They take it through a one-way portal home and come back when the high wears off. A Krakaren borough boss brews the drug. The crews are dwarf conductors, grapple porters, Jikininki janitors and mantaur engineers sealed in their cabs, at least one of them a worshipper of Grull. At 435 the Kravyad work dark magic on the crews before the portal to the depot. None of them have the homes they remember: the floor gave them their memories.

The railway is a company. Madison of human resources tells the crews that overtime is mandatory, and manages benefits for the Kravyad and the six station mimics. The Kravyad are blue, six-armed, a little like nagas: they hypnotise each crew as it gets off, keep it in a stupor between shifts so nobody asks for time off, and are paid by eating a dwarf or two a shift. A gold armband marks a troublemaker as fair game. The crews' portal at 435 lives only as long as its Kravyad does. The crews dream of the dormitories at station 60, which is a cobwebbed platform with nothing behind it. Widget, a grease gremlin, works a watchtower in the trainyard. And the monsters who miss their vial go into withdrawal, and stop being anybody.

The floor is a political cartoon. The Krakaren making the drug is a caricature of a real creature, a collective mind whose better name is the Apothecary, and the Pooka handing it out stand for the Plenty, a goat people who invented the tunnelling system the whole universe talks through. The railway company tells its crews that overtime is mandatory and lets the Kravyad eat the troublemakers. At station 75, Growler Gary keeps a bar he cannot leave, and comes back to life every time he dies. The crews believe in homes at station 60 that were never built.

The monsters get on at the stations. When the doors open, packs of Drek pour in, and a pack is said to strip an elephant to the bone in under five seconds. The Jikininki in the janitors' car are well-behaved until somebody bleeds. The tunnel is too tight to jump from a moving train, and there is a next train behind.

Packs of monsters board at every stop, and fighting on a train means holding a car with the doors on both sides. The third rail on the track is bare. A prize can be a trap: a porter's suitcase can be full of burning ants. The engineers are mantaur berserkers who will turn on anyone in Grull's name. And the crews warn every passenger to get off at 433, because beyond it nothing is safe.

The crews tell everyone to get off at 433 because the Terminus there is a station mimic, one of six, and they are ravenous. A monster that misses its dose gets the DTs: in the first stage half of them drop dead, and in the second their strength doubles, they stop thinking and attack anything, and the transfer stations no longer keep them out. Those that die become ghouls. The ghouls were meant to be caged and carried off to the abyss, but the system has broken: the trainyards are overrun, the walls are breached, and the ghouls are walking up the lines towards the stairwell stations. On more and more lines the trains have stopped coming.

The trains have stopped on every track, so most of the floor is on foot. Every stairwell station is held by something. Jikininki gather at 12 and blister ghouls at 72, both pouring out of ghoul generators powered by soul crystals; every non-undead mob that dies anywhere on the floor births another blister ghoul. Wrath ghouls collect at 36. At 48 the festering ghouls have pulled themselves together into a province boss too big to leave its room. Station 24 is empty, so far. The station mimic still waits at 433, and the DT monsters are on the tracks.

The DTs have a third stage. Monsters in it sprout tentacles of their own and run faster than ever, and when they die they burst into thousands of rice-sized Krakaren that grow hour on hour. The young Krakaren have gathered at every station 24 and stay there. Generators at 12 and 72 keep spawning ghouls, the 48s are held by a province boss, wrath ghouls left to gather at a 36 make another, and the station mimic waits at 433. The trains are dead; the tracks belong to whatever is walking them.

The Tangle is destroying itself. In the stations a round section of floor falls away, and up through the hole come the Krakaren, human-sized now, without end. The generators at 12 and 72 still spawn, the province bosses still hold their rooms, and the escape tunnels are opening with gravity that may not point the way it should. In eighteen hours the stairwell portals open, for six. After that the charges blow.

layers.label: Every fifth stop · the vial door

floors.name: The Bubbles
floors.premise: Floor five! Every one of you is sealed in a bubble: a little world with four quadrants, four castles and a civilisation that was minding its own business. Liberate all four castles and the stairs open. Don't, and you don't leave. Every box on this floor comes with water-breathing scrolls. I'm sure that's nothing.

recap.title: A bubble full of sand
recap.text: The stairs drop them into a sandstorm inside bubble 543, and Carl finds every bounty on him doubled. Each bubble is a sealed world of four quadrants: land, water, air and underground. Each quadrant has a castle, and the stairs open only when all four fall. Theirs is the air quadrant, a desert bowl under a dome with a flying castle called the Wasteland near the top of it, and dirigible gnomes who bomb everything below. Donut takes Glass Cannon and somehow misses its constitution bonus. Mordecai is a skyfowl now, the first body near his own in a very long time. In Hump Town, a camel town, a changeling boy named Skarn rents out his telescope, and the town hall keeps a secret that stops the gnomes bombing it. Being stepped on by a god pays well: a toe ring that sticks to ceilings, a lizard-foot tattoo under Carl's eye, and Pawna's Tears, a goddess's potion that adds five to any skill. The other crawlers in the quadrant are thin on the ground. Louis drove his mother's roofless minivan into the dungeon. His friend Firas is with him, and so is Langley's team, six Helsinki car salesmen who all became archers. In the Spit and Swallow a changeling prostitute called Juice Box sits on Louis's lap and stays there. Carl and Katia build the Royal Chariot, a tracked sand buggy. The recap shows how Ifechi died: Lucia Mar turned Florin's own shotgun back onto her. On the new board Carl is second.

recap.title: A head, a lie, and a dreadnaught
recap.text: Under the town hall, guarded by changelings wearing camel shapes, is Wynne, the gnome commandant's uncle, held hostage for the peace. A changeling called Henrik has been drugging him and wearing faces he knows, trying to make him give up a spell that would put flesh on a tomb-ghost called Quetzalcoatlus. Crawlers from the underground quadrant reach him first and kill him at his own request. The town hall burns, and Carl blames it on frogs. New sponsors arrive. Carl's is a pacifist network nobody can explain, Donut's a pet-toy company, and Katia's is the Squim Conglomerate, the corporation that ran last season. A borough boss's description gives away what is buried in the necropolis under the bowl: the Gate of the Feral Gods, an artifact so far above this floor's grade that the world freezes for half a second while the game reconciles it. Henrik carries a pocket watch linked to the Commandant's, and Carl suspects the watches are pieces of the Gate. So they run a con. Donut raises Wynne's head with Second Chance, Katia supplies the body under it and plays Henrik, and Donut presents herself as the famed healer of Queen Anne, carrying a potion that is Mountain Dew. The gnome ambassador takes them up in his balloon. Mid-air they hijack it, Donut holes the bottom of the basket to drop its crew, and Carl puts missiles into the Wasteland's bombs before they can fall on Hump Town. The dreadnaught breaks apart. All that stays up is a single house under a balloon, with the Commandant and his little daughter inside.

recap.title: Maggie, a goose, and a commercial
recap.text: Chris Andrews walks up at last, level thirty-five and made of lava rock, and something is wrong with him. Juice Box touches him and feels two people inside. Katia's sponsor sends an emergency box of petrifying bolts, and she puts one in his head just as he raises a celestial grenade. It is Maggie My, reborn as a Scree, a worm that rides the living. Chris is awake behind his own eyes, and through Elle he asks them to kill him. Donut will not let Carl kill a friend, so she drops Chris through a hole into a sealed chamber under the street. Carl flies a stolen biplane into the floating house and finds the Commandant half-eaten on his kitchen table and his daughter Bonnie making lemonade. The killer is Denise, a feral goose in a bonnet whose aura switches off magic. With the house sinking, Carl holds her head in the kitchen sink and Donut hits the garbage disposal, and the air quadrant is theirs. Carl strips the house and gives Bonnie her own bed back in town. Then Loita, the Bloom agent who replaced Zev, pulls them out for an infomercial for Donut's robot doll. She boasts that Zev was brought back into line through what was done to her mother and aunts. Carl has shimmed the doll's back panel open with his own thumbnail and sets it beside her on the couch. It explodes, and Loita dies in an undersea trailer whose window holds. Carl has used an old Cookbook note, and he adds one of his own: One. A Syndicate liaison cannot prove intent and has to let them go. Five days have passed, and Katia has been running things without them.

recap.title: The sandcastle and the sharktopus
recap.text: Katia has flown the half-house down to the land quadrant, where Gwen, a blunt Canadian fighter, has been waiting a day to wash the Mad Dune Mage's sandcastle away. They go in the hard way instead. The mage, Ghazi, is a lovesick scholar in a bathrobe who opened the Gate hoping a god would make a stage-play heroine love him. What came through married him to a sand ooze. The other half of that soul sits in the fountain, in the crystal head of a love doll. Carl knocks him out, takes the winding box, and burns the ooze's core from the ceiling. The castle comes down; Katia carries Ghazi out and kills him for his notes; Tran opens the drain, and Carl and Donut are flushed a hundred and fifty metres deep into the water quadrant, which Donut will never forgive. The doll's head wakes up as Samantha, half of a banished goddess, and Donut hires her as a trainer. Ghazi's notes show that the watches can aim the Gate anywhere, including the city of Larracos on the ninth floor. In the water quadrant a flooded submarine is pumping the ocean into the necropolis. Inside it are Henrik's body and his watch, and a note saying Quetzalcoatlus dies to electricity. Then the sub is swallowed by Lusca, a sharktopus the size of a mountain, with two commentators calling it live. Vadim runs for the last escape pod, and it does not save him. Carl sets a bloodlust bomb off among the babies in Lusca's mouth, fires his shell down her throat, and Katia saws through her brain. Then Carl uses the Gate to carry the three of them to the beach. An ocean comes through with them, and a feral god gets out behind.

recap.title: Orthrus
recap.text: Seven of the ninth floor's factions have sued to take the Gate from Carl and lost. The AI pays him seven times over, in stock certificates and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers, and Mordecai starts to worry that it is going primal. Elsewhere a god walks through bubbles on fire, shouting for Orthrus. That is Emberus, and the feral god Carl let out is Orthrus, his dead son's two-headed puppy. Orthrus is the size of a building, fragile, and the one god down here who can die. Maggie gets loose again inside Chris. Underground, the last two tomb raiders connect the lightning panel under the necropolis at Carl's word, knowing the current will kill them, and Quetzalcoatlus burns out with them. The bubble pops. Donut rides into the storm in the flying house to keep the puppy healed. Two quests land at once: bring Orthrus to Emberus, or kill him for a prize. Quan Ch takes the second. Carl flies a gnome biplane with Donut burning a Meat Hooks scroll behind him to lead the puppy out, and Quan Ch shoots them down. Falling, Carl swears himself to Emberus and throws the celestial grenade he took from Maggie. The god arrives as a head the size of a city, takes his dog and goes. For sixty seconds Carl cannot be hurt, and Quan Ch cannot see it. Quan launches away mid-punch without his left arm. It has three rings on it, and the gold one says For Daddy.

recap.title: Emptying the bubbles
recap.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now. There is a blood tithe, a sun shrine in the saferoom, fire on his fists, and a quest to kill the god's twin brother Hellik by the twelfth floor. The Gate becomes a lifeboat. A bubble's survivors gather at their own Desperado Club door, the pieces are passed from hand to hand inside the club, and they step through to Hump Town, leaving a feral god behind in the world they fled. Imani refuses to leave a single person behind; about fifteen hundred get out, and Borant rules the trick legal. Katia says she will split off on the next floor to gather the scattered Daughters before Eva does. Florin, who has lost everything, pledges his gun. Then comes the finale Carl has been announcing out loud: a feral god for the ninth floor. It is a decoy. Chris, with Maggie inside him, throws the winding box off the bowl. It is a fake Katia swapped in during a hug. Carl drinks a phase potion, reaches into Chris's head and pulls the worm out; it burrows into Carl and a second potion throws it out through his neck, and Mongo eats Maggie My. Chris says his brother's name. The real Gate opens in the water quadrant, and a bubble's ocean, timed charges and a feeding frenzy of sharks pour into Larracos's faction market. Tens of thousands of NPCs drown, along with the mercenaries the factions meant to hire. Juice Box goes through with the water to warn her people, and announces she is marrying Louis. Carl tops the leaderboard, holds up the Ring of Divine Suffering for the cameras, and swears to kill every hunter on the next floor. On the ruined surface, Odette's people take Bea out of a Seattle camp.

floors.previously: In the Iron Tangle: Carl found a book that twenty-four dead crawlers wrote in before him, and he has been insufferable ever since. They stole a train, rescued six hundred crawlers with a bartender's hands, and dropped a war god through a portal while the Maestro was driving it. Hekla tried to steal Donut, it cost her her life, and Katia wears a golden skull now. Fire Brandy rode her train into the pit so everyone else could live. Carl wrote a promise in the margins: I will break them all. Cute. Now: your own little world, in a bubble.

steps.text: The floor is 1,172 bubbles laid out like a sheet of bubble wrap, with a little more than a hundred and fifty crawlers sealed inside each one. Every bubble is its own world, split into four quadrants: land, sea, air and subterranean. Each quadrant has one castle, and there are more than four thousand on the floor, no two alike. Take the throne room or kill the quadrant's boss and the castle is yours. The stairwell is in the throne room, but it stays shut until all four castles in the bubble have fallen. Until your own castle falls you cannot leave your quadrant; after that you may cross over to help your neighbours. When the fourth castle goes the bubble pops, and you may leave it, though not into a bubble that has not popped yet. Reaching the stairs in the top ten has a price: every bounty on you is doubled.

The floor is 1,172 bubbles laid out like a sheet of bubble wrap, each a sealed world of four quadrants with one castle apiece, and the stairwell in each throne room stays shut until all four castles in the bubble have fallen. Bubble 543 is done. Its four castles are down, the bubble has popped, and all four stairwells are open. A popped bubble may be left, but only for another that has popped too.

Bubble 543 is a dome, four or five kilometres to the top, and the crawlers arrive in a sandstorm inside the air quadrant. That is a desert bowl sitting on top of the Necropolis of Anser, a tomb so tall that the ground and the sea are far below. Hump Town is built against the bowl's wall behind patchwork metal, its streets laid out in nested half-circles like a rainbow, and its city hall is for camels only. Cave mouths in the sand lead down into the subterranean quadrant underneath. The air castle is a speck high above, brushing the ceiling of the dome.

From the telescope on Skarn's roof the whole bowl is visible: almost a circle, a little more than three miles from edge to edge. A second town mirrors Hump Town on the opposite wall, the Bactrians'. Between them lie dunes, cave mouths, metal wrecks and big shapes patrolling the badlands. The speck in the sky is the Wasteland, the gnomes' castle: a jagged slab of ground torn out of the earth, held up by five colossal balloons inside a magic shield, with a house on top and corrugated shacks around its edges. Far below, Gwen reports, the land quadrant is an island at sea level with three villages, and the Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage is built into the side of the tomb behind four rings of walls. A coral reef rings the island. Nobody has seen the sea castle. The tomb itself has many entrances, none of them open, and it looks like a maze inside.

The bowl is a little more than three miles across, sitting on top of the Necropolis of Anser, with Hump Town against one wall and what is left of the Bactrian town against the other. The Wasteland still hangs near the ceiling on its five balloons. Down at sea level the land quadrant is an island with three villages, the Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage built into the tomb behind four rings of walls, and a coral reef around the shore. The sea castle is a submarine, and Chris has taken it. Taking it has let the water in: the tomb's entrances have sealed, and the catacombs under the bowl are filling up with nowhere for the sea to go.

The bowl sits on top of the Necropolis of Anser, a tomb tall enough to carry a desert, with Hump Town on one wall and the Bactrian ruins on the other. The Wasteland is gone. Its bombs went up under it and the dreadnaught came apart in the air; all that still floats is a single house under one balloon. Below, the island holds three villages and the Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage behind its four walls, inside a ring of reef. The sea castle has already fallen to Chris, and the water it let in is flooding the catacombs.

The air and sea castles have fallen, and now the land castle has too. The Sandcastle of the Mad Dune Mage came down with the drain open, and Carl and Donut went down with it, flushed through the necropolis and out a hundred and fifty metres deep into the sea quadrant. The water quadrant is open ocean around the island, deep and full of sharks. The air quadrant's bowl still sits at the top of the necropolis, with Hump Town on one wall, the Bactrian ruins on the other, and what was left of the Wasteland's house now landed on the island below. That leaves the subterranean quadrant: the maze inside the tomb, still flooding.

Bubble 543 is popped and all four stairwells are passable. At the top of the necropolis is the bowl, with Hump Town on one wall, the Bactrian ruins on the other and nothing left in the sky. At its foot are the island and the rubble of the sandcastle, and around it the sea, part of which the Gate has just emptied onto the beach.

Seen from the air, bubble 543 is one blister on a sheet of bubble wrap that runs to the horizon. Between the bubbles are ravines of dark, and the domes on either side are opaque where they are still sealed: one popped neighbour holds a giant cactus, another a curved concrete structure. Inside 543 the bowl still sits on top of the necropolis with Hump Town and the Bactrian ruins on its walls, the island and the sandcastle's rubble at its foot, the sea all around.

Hump Town belongs to the Dromedarians: eight-foot camels who walk on two legs, wear headscarves and robes, and talk like biker bouncers. A toll gets you in, the city hall is for Dromedarians only, and the town's economy is mostly brothels. Some of the women on Hump Street change shape as you pass, into a human or a skyfowl. The camels are locked in a three-way stalemate with the Bactrians and the Dirigible Gnomes, and are perfectly content to smoke and drink while they wait for it to boil over. The gnomes hold the castle in the sky.

Three peoples share the bowl. The Dromedarians hold Hump Town, the Bactrians hold the town on the opposite wall, and the Dirigible Gnomes hold the sky. According to Skarn, a changeling boy with a telescope, the gnomes leave Hump Town alone because of something kept in its town hall that their leader wants kept safe, and the Bactrians have the same arrangement. Down on the island the land quadrant has scorpion-men with nipple rings, giant snakes and spiders, and bird things with chainsaws.

The peace is a hostage. Under Hump Town's town hall the camels hold Wynne, uncle of the gnomes' Commandant Kane, and that is why the bombs fall somewhere else. But many of the camels are not camels: changelings have taken their shapes inside the hall. One of them, Henrik, has been drugging Wynne and wearing faces he knows, trying to get a spell out of him that would put flesh back on Quetzalcoatlus, the ghost that haunts the tomb. The Bactrians had the same deal, and Carl suspects the crawlers over there broke it, which is why the gnomes flattened their town.

The gnomes' Commandant Kane is dead, half-eaten on his own kitchen table in the last floating house. The killer was Denise, a feral goose in a bonnet whose aura switches magic off, and she is dead too, drowned in the kitchen sink. Kane's daughter Bonnie is the one gnome left from the house. Carl has stripped it, and brought her own bed down for her in Hump Town. In Hump Town itself the Dromedarians and the changelings among them carry on much as before. The town hall is ash.

The Dromedarians hold Hump Town, the Bactrian town is rubble, and the gnomes' castle has fallen out of the sky, leaving Bonnie in Hump Town. Inside the necropolis there are settlements the crawlers never saw: the Nude Glabers lived there, and the flood the sea castle let in has drowned them. Their bodies drift through the catacombs.

Sandstorms that blot out the sky; Hump Town raises a town-wide awning against them. A gnome castle overhead, in a stalemate with the towns below that the description says could boil over any day. Tunnels down into the subterranean quadrant with traps in them. And the clock, because about a hundred and fifty crawlers to a bubble means most of the help is underpowered, and four castles have to fall before anybody leaves.

The gnomes bomb what is under them; Hump Town is spared only because of something in its town hall. Sandstorms blot out the sky, and Hump Town raises a town-wide awning against them. The tunnels down into the subterranean quadrant are trapped. On the island below there are giant snakes and spiders, scorpion-men and bird things with chainsaws. And the clock is running on four castles.

The gnomes have shown what they can do. The Wasteland drifted over the Bactrian town and bombed it to rubble, and nobody in Hump Town knows why. Sandstorms still blot out the sky, the tunnels down into the tomb are trapped, and the clock is running on four castles.

A second, smaller sun rises and chases the first across the sky, and the heat it brings makes it hard to breathe. The gnome airships bomb anything under them, as the Bactrian town found out. Sandstorms still blot out the sky. The tunnels down into the tomb are trapped and the subterranean quadrant is a maze. Quetzalcoatlus haunts the tomb.

The tomb is flooding. Since the sea castle fell, water has been pouring into the catacombs, and the entrances have closed behind it, so there is nowhere for the sea to go. Above, the heat of the second sun, the sandstorms and the gnome airships carry on. Quetzalcoatlus still haunts the tomb.

The sea quadrant is open water full of sharks and jellyfish, and something far worse: Lusca, the Octo-Shark Brood Mother Queen, a sharktopus the size of a mountain with her babies carried in her mouth, broadcast live by two commentators as she swallows a submarine whole. The tomb is still flooding, Quetzalcoatlus still haunts it, and the heat and the storms have not let up.

Lusca is dead, but the Gate let something out when it carried Carl, Donut and Katia to the beach. That is Orthrus, a feral god: a two-headed puppy the size of a building, fragile, and the one god down here who can die. Behind him comes his master. Emberus walks through the bubbles on fire, shouting for his dog. A lightning storm is building. Quetzalcoatlus still haunts the tomb.

The bubble has popped, Quetzalcoatlus has burned out, and Emberus has come for his dog and gone. What is left is the floor outside: thousands of bubbles, some still sealed, some popped and open to whatever was in them, and crawlers who will shoot down a biplane for a quest's prize. Get to a saferoom, or get down the stairs.

floors.name: The Hunting Grounds
floors.premise: Welcome to the Hunting Grounds! A jungle the size of a small country, with towns, elves, dryads, and a brand-new feature: people. Rich, bored people from all over the galaxy have bought a licence to come down here and shoot you for sport. They start at level thirty. You don't get a say. Run, hide, or make it interesting.

recap.title: Zockau burns
recap.text: At registration, a Syndicate liaison asks Carl to hand back the Gate of the Feral Gods, and Carl asks for a lawyer. The lawyer is Quasar, a Null who trades the Gate away for four free cretin mercenaries (Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton and Very Sullen) and two spells that copy its tricks: Bomo gets a jump to the stairwell, and the Sledge gets something called Zerzura that nobody explains. Carl takes the bomb specialisation, Agent Provocateur. Donut is a Legendary Diva whose spells only work if she sings them in key, and she cannot sing in key. Mordecai is a knee-high Pocket Kuma who has to jump to reach doorknobs. Katia and Chris leave with the caravans. Then, hours before the hunters are released, Bomo drops Carl and Donut on the stairwell steps in Zockau, the city where every hunter on the floor is waiting. Carl marks them with the Ring of Divine Suffering, kills them, and takes their stats. He lines a street of pubs with barrel bombs, and the Desperado Club's front comes down with hunters trapped inside. He gets out full of crossbow bolts and wakes in a cart pulled by Bianca, Prepotente's hellspawn goat, with Miriam Dom stroking his hair. She is a vampire now. Thirty-four hunters, and more than two hundred and fifty other casualties. It bothers him less than it should.

recap.title: Point Mongo
recap.text: Every hunter Carl kills pays in gold and a severed hand, and the hands can be spent at the prize counter of the Butcher's Masquerade, a party the high elves throw at the floor's end for the top fifty crawlers. The ring leaves a spiderweb tattoo on his elbow, the mark of the Night Wyrm's cult, and something at the back of his mind has begun to rush like a river. Guilds go live. Hunter Vrah, a mantis who wears her kills' heads on her back and whose little sister Carl blew out of the sky in Zockau, pins a note to his door: the Hive is hunting him. Across the river, an ursine town bans dinosaurs, so Donut blows its mayor down a slope with Astral Paw, takes the town and renames it Point Mongo. Then Mongo bolts into the jungle with her on his back, straight to an all-female pack of his own kind led by a one-eyed matriarch called Kiwi, and settles the introductions in the obvious way. Back in town Donut breaks down. Everybody always leaves her: Miss Beatrice, Katia, now Mongo, and Carl keeps doing more dangerous things. Carl promises he will never leave her behind, on the ninth floor or any other. Quasar bargains a secret licence for Signet's show to continue past this floor. Then Signet herself walks out of the trees with a bound hunter across her caterpillar's saddle and a war party behind her.

recap.title: Beatrice
recap.text: Signet's story, as she tells it: her naiad mother was murdered by a dissident Confederacy with high-elf help, and her half-sister Imogen now rules the high elves. She has gathered an army of were-castors, bush elves, a caterpillar sage and a tattooing tortoise to cut both of them out. Part one of Vengeance of the Daughter is to take Fort Freedom, the old river palace. A dead hunter's map shows the floor carved into hunting territories, and two outfits have put their claim on Carl and Donut: the Hive and the Skull Empire. Their third and last sponsor signs on, the Apothecary, a collective mind. Then they are pulled up to orbit for Odette's show, and she tells them Bea is alive. Bounty hunters were about to sell her to Borant to be made into a country boss, and Odette had her taken off the planet first and is using her to blackmail Borant. On the couch Beatrice appears drugged, thin and confused, asks why Carl isn't wearing pants, and is surprised the cat can talk. Off air Donut tells her she was going to sell her, and that she is not her person any more. Carl is. The moment the broadcast ends, a court makes Borant independent of its government, and the Valtay take fifty-one percent of it. Donut, it slips out, helped smuggle Valtay agents to Zev and something called the Borant Emancipation Front. Lexis warns them that Queen Imogen is a country boss built to wipe out the top of the leaderboard at the party.

recap.title: Fort Freedom
recap.text: Katia finally leaves the party, though not the circle: the Royal Court joins Imani's guild, Safehome Yolanda, and Katia moves in next door with her own crew. Carl's fans vote him a booth at CrawlCon, which no active crawler has attended in a century. Elves from the Dream shell the town with a catapult. Carl straps missiles to Samantha's head and throws her at them, and marks one of their hunters, an accountant who won his place at fantasy hunter camp. The ring levels up. Donut takes a bracelet that casts Fireball, and Carl's anger is starting to scare her. Word comes that Langley and his whole team of archers are dead, their heads on Vrah's back. At Fort Freedom the Confederacy's defence is a joke, and Signet's amphibious team goes in the back while Samantha draws the guards to the front. What comes out of the throne room is a truck-sized eryops called Claude Sludgington the Fourth, with Samantha inside it. Carl's shell sends it straight up instead of sideways, Donut's fireball finds its belly, and Mongo eats his way out through the other side. The kill lands before the quest does, and the achievement is called Premature Questjaculation. Part two arrives: kill Queen Imogen at the Masquerade. The Recital quest names the thing that has been eating Point Mongo's neighbours. Big Tina, an allosaurus city boss in pink feathers.

recap.title: CrawlCon
recap.text: Just as they reach the next village, Carl is pulled away to CrawlCon, leaving Donut in a town whose new mayor is Lucia Mar. He judges a children's drawing contest. The moderator of his panel is Circe Took, a hive queen, Vrah's mother and the mother of the hunter he killed. His own guards' vape smoke has been drugged. He puts his bare feet on the table, bores her on air, and when she tries to cut him off, a robed woman in the back row stops her: a spokeswoman for the Apothecary, his sponsor. Circe cleaves the table in half and storms out. Carl asks the audience how best to kill her daughter, and they tell him: seven warrior sisters, and a male who trades in Zockau. Back on the floor, Lucia has trapped the saferoom doors with teleports and Vrah's hunters are waiting outside. Carl comes back invisible, sets off every trap in town at once, and feeds Lucia a stuffed-cat decoy that makes her spring her own trap. A wheeled bomb kills three mantises, one of them tears her own sister apart, and Donut raises the heads on Vrah's back, Langley's among them, to bite her. Carl rams an arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea into Vrah's neck. For her kind there are two cures: gelding, or passing it on. The last mantis on the floor, Edict, is a gentle accountant with no good choices left, and he punches Carl in a saferoom to be teleported away to die. The recap shows Donut's fight with Lucia: Lucia talking to an invisible youth assistant called Alexandro, and Donut dropping Cici's head through a hole in the floor.

recap.title: Miriam
recap.text: At the autograph tables Carl's replacement sponsor is announced: the Plenty, the caprid collective. A naga reporter called Nihit tells him he is cheating, and Carl stabs him in the neck with a magical Sharpie. If Carl survives the crawl, that will mean a warrant, and a warrant can be sold. The Plenty and the Apothecary both send protection against vampirism on the same day. The next day Miriam Dom calls for help. Big Tina was an ursine child, the best dancer at a secret ballet recital, when the nine-tier attack came. Her cleric father had just beaten her mother on the stage for teaching it, and the attack turned the town's women into dinosaurs. Tina was the only child it changed. Tina's mother is Kiwi, and Tina's mind is gone. Miriam bit her in a fight with Viscount Fog, an elite vampire hunter, and now vampirism is spreading through every dinosaur in the forest. Carl fights his way to her through a vampire pterosaur boss, Fog's own mount, and finds her in a clearing, pinned under Prepotente's arm. He is paralysed and fragile, and in the fight his own Ring of Divine Suffering marked her: while she lives he cannot heal. She is the source of the plague. She asks Carl to kill her before Prepotente wakes. He will not. He waits with her until the sun comes up, and she dies with her head on her boy's frozen shoulder. Carl puts his own ring on behind his back as she goes, and takes three points of intelligence from her death. Donut wakes Prepotente, who screams at what is left of her and swallows his ring. A world quest follows: fifty Odious Creepers, dead by sunset.

recap.title: Brambles
recap.text: Donut charms Kiwi with a potion, and Carl works out that the Plenty arranged Miriam's death to protect Prepotente. The guilds hunt creepers with Mordecai's weedkiller: Louis sprays it from the flying house, Carl lobs it with a stolen elven trebuchet, and Prepotente kills ten. Then the queen's familiar appears in a curtained litter, promises Donut a dance at the Masquerade, and fires lightning at Mongo. Donut takes it for him. It is Ferdinand. The last two creepers sit in Zockau, where only the hunters can reach them, so the quest fails, and the punishment is Gehenna Bramble: walls of thorns that boil the blood, spreading across the floor at four and a half kilometres an hour. Saferoom time must now be earned by killing. A drunk hunter teleported into Carl's lap says the AI is ignoring court orders and going primal, and the ring levels again. Carl works out that the brambles will finish covering the map at the high elves' castle at the floor's last minute. Circe Took has sponsored the god Diwata, and Carl's other sponsor, the pacifist network, slips him a potion for Donut. He bribes her to take it with a nipple ring, and pierces his own first. Then Quasar's real plan comes out. Zerzura moves a whole town, NPCs and all, one floor down, and the Hump Town changelings and Bonnie need to be inside a town when the Sledge casts it. The only town left standing is the castle.

recap.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
recap.text: Orren the liaison has Carl brought in, clumsily warns him that some liaisons disagree with their own governments, and lets Quasar in to talk. The guild raids hunters to thin them before the party. Carl kills a worshipper of his own god by accident and wears Shunned over his head. Diwata bursts out of a hunter, marks Carl for death and runs straight past him to Vrah, to cure her in the only way that works. Five Apothecary boxes addressed to Donut arrive through other crawlers: a tiara, sheet music, a hammer, a metal rod, a recharge scroll, each marked with a small seven, as if they expect everyone else to be dead. Carl lies to Signet that her assault must wait for his signal. Then the party begins. The castle is a white cube of carved oak, which Elle calls the Sugar Cube. Imogen appears in their carriage with Ifechi's face. She is Ifechi's twin, remade as a country boss. The whole Masquerade sits under Apito's celestial peace seal: whoever breaks it is fed to the Nothing, and if nobody does, the queen earns a goddess's boon. In the ballroom Empress D'nadia judges the contests, Chaco runs the prize counter, Vrah promises a present, and Katia has to be held back from Eva. Lucia sits against a wall chewing her nails. Then Signet walks in. Apito herself invited her, as a test for her sister, and she says no host has ever won that boon.

recap.title: The seal breaks
recap.text: Chaco, who regrets whatever he did to Mordecai, sells Carl a shrink wand, a lore book and a case of Feather Falls for his hunters' hands, and warns him that this place always makes you turn on your own party. Mongo moonwalks for the judges. Florin tells the others there are several people in Lucia's head, some of them children, and that the dog is the key. Donut charms Ferdinand into her party. Imogen comes in with blood down her gown: Gideon and nearly thirty crawlers waiting in the trees are dead because Carl asked them to wait there. Prudence is dead outside. The mantises have taken the flying house. Donut sings her mother's song, All Eyes on Me, and every creature in the room is charmed. Big Tina dances at last, with thirty velociraptors in paper sea-creature costumes behind her. Then Signet opens her own throat. Her blood wakes her tattoos for good, the floor opens and the Nothing takes her, and the seal is broken. The Sledge finishes Zerzura, and the whole castle goes to the ninth floor with the changelings, Bonnie, Tina, and Kiwi, whom Donut's potion has turned back into a pregnant bear her daughter finally recognises. Everyone else drops into a cage fight under a dome of thorns while Thunderstruck plays. Mongo and Kiwi bring down Vrah. Donut's Laundry Day strips the god off Circe Took, and her own children eat her. Imogen falls. So do Firas, Gwen, Horton and the Popov brothers, who split into two babies and are carried out of the dungeon to safety. Katia finds Eva alive under the bugs and kills her, and Eva's last act is to put the Crown of the Sepsis Whore on Katia's head. Now only one of Katia and Donut can leave the ninth floor. Donut's fans have bought the Royal Court a seat in Faction Wars, and Carl uses the last of his airtime to tell the galaxy how to vote.

floors.previously: In the Bubbles: every crawler got a sealed little world, and Carl got an artifact he had no business owning, the Gate of the Feral Gods. He hijacked a gnome balloon with a cat and a severed head, drowned a goose in a garbage disposal, blew up a PR agent with a toy, and was swallowed by a sharktopus. Chris came back with Maggie My in his skull; Mongo ate her. Carl swore himself to Emberus to survive a plane crash, emptied the bubbles through the Gate, and flooded Larracos, four floors down, to make a point. Now the hunters are coming. He asked for it.

steps.text: The floor runs seventeen days, and this time the crawlers are not alone down here. Hunters have paid to come in from outside, and they are here to hunt crawlers for their gear. There are 360 of them on deck at the start, sequestered in the city of Zockau and released after a thirty-hour grace period, with registration held open to the last moment. A hunter traditionally starts at level 30; this season they have been given twenty extra and start at 50. Their minions and traps are already out in the jungle. There are 2,344 exits to the next floor: at least one unguarded in Zockau, more in the valley beyond it, some near city bosses and bigger mobs, the rest hidden. The last sponsorship slots open for bidding on arrival.

Seventeen days, and hunters on the map as purple dots. They start at level 50 and hunt crawlers for their gear, and their traps and minions are already in the jungle. The floor has one named city, held by a single race. When the hunters arrive, one of them kills its NPC leader and sets up as Grand, the title for the mayor of the biggest settlements, and after that the city guards attack crawlers on sight. It is the only city where the hunters can do this. Of 2,344 exits, at least one sits unguarded in that city and more lie in the valley beyond it; the rest are hidden or near the bosses.

Every hunter killed pays out a Hunter Killer box: gold, and a severed hand. The hands are tickets, spent at a prize counter that opens at the Butcher’s Masquerade, a party at the end of the floor. The cheapest prize costs one hand. Only the top 50 crawlers are invited, each with a plus one, and the hunters attend too. Guilds go live: a charter from a Bopca costs 500,000 gold and lets several parties pool a common area, and parties are now capped at thirty crawlers. Viewers can no longer listen in on private messages. Over a thousand hunters are now in the dungeon, all at level 50 or more, and they show as purple dots. The one named city is theirs, and its guards attack crawlers on sight.

Hunters may no longer talk to anyone outside the dungeon, which cuts off the tips they were being fed. Crawlers in the top 1,000 can now see their own rank, because only the top 50 are invited to the Butcher’s Masquerade, where the hands of dead hunters buy prizes at the counter. Guilds pool parties of up to thirty. Sponsors may sell their stakes from the next floor. Hunters still come up as purple dots, still start at level 50, and still hold the one named city, where the guards attack crawlers on sight.

Saferooms are timed now, for crawlers and hunters alike. Entering one starts a blood bar counting down. A full bar buys ten hours of rest, and at zero you are teleported out to somewhere random. Empty, you cannot enter a saferoom, guildhall or pub at all. The bar fills by killing, and it counts back to the start of the floor, so anyone who has killed nothing arrives with it empty. Hunter hands still buy prizes at the Masquerade counter for the top 50, and guilds still pool parties of thirty.

The Butcher’s Masquerade starts thirty hours before collapse and runs four or five hours. When the countdown hits zero, the top 50 are teleported straight into the ballroom of the High Elf castle, with plus-one tokens for one more crawler each. The hunters attend in the same room, but they are actually somewhere else in the castle: nobody can hurt anybody. No magic, no weapons, no explosives, no traps and no inventory in the ballrooms. Pets and NPC companions wait in staging areas and appear only as extras. There is a pet beauty contest, a talent show, a buffet and a prize booth that takes hunter hands or crawler scalps. Queen Imogen guarantees safe passage. Afterwards crawlers leave by the south entrance and hunters by the north, and they may kill each other again. Saferooms still run on the blood bar, filled by killing.

The floor is a jungle, almost identical in layout and size to the third floor, but the old ruins have been swallowed by hundreds of years of foliage. Leaves the size of kites, rain that drums down and stops all at once, air so wet it is hard to breathe; through the canopy there is no ceiling to be seen. The crawlers come out of their changing rooms beside a trail, a few steps from a Medium Dryad Settlement: a ten-foot bamboo wall, and inside a German-style village tangled up with treehouses, shops and pubs fixed to the trunks, monkeys in the branches and the gold spire of a Club Vanquisher against the back wall. The hunters’ city, Zockau, is all the way to the north.

The map is a round world of jungle, the same every season, with one named city and dozens of unnamed towns. Zockau sits in the north near the edge, overlooking a clear valley stocked with low-level monsters for the hunters to train on. All the way to the southeast, in the thickest jungle, is the high elf city. Between the old city and the elves’ jungle winds a river, bridged at intervals. Zockau itself looks like the downtown of a small American town from the 1950s: a manicured park around a stairwell whose light rises fifty feet to the artificial ceiling, a street of seven pubs, and at the end the three-storey, mid-century front of the Desperado Club. From outside the city the border is opaque.

The floor is about 100,000 square kilometres, close to Iceland in size and even in shape: four hundred-odd kilometres north to south and three hundred-odd east to west. Zockau sits at the top. The river meanders from the northeast corner to the southwest, about five hundred kilometres end to end, splitting into tributaries and lakes, and cuts the map in two like a snake. The main road runs out of Zockau straight to the river, crosses, and ends about halfway into the jungle; the caravans travel it. At least a dozen bridges cross the river. The high elves hold the southeast.

The floor is about the size and shape of Iceland, cut from northeast to southwest by a river that runs about two hundred and fifty feet wide where the main road crosses it on a covered wooden bridge. About ten bridges have been knocked down. Over that bridge, sixty kilometres from Zockau, is Point Mongo, a big, tidy ursine town of cobblestones and clipped shrubs with the jungle pressing in around it. Upriver stands Fort Freedom, the old naiad river palace. A dead hunter’s map, crayoned on the back of a kids’ menu, carves the floor into hunting grounds: the Hive holds the bottom left, the Dream holds the country around Point Mongo, the Skull Empire the southeast near the elves, and the unaffiliated hunters the land around Zockau.

From above the canopy there is nothing but trees in every direction, the river winding through them like a snake, and to the south the heads of long-necked dinosaurs poking up above the treeline. The southwest corner holds hot springs and lava tubes. Upriver from Point Mongo, where the river is a mile and a half wide, Fort Freedom rises a quarter of a mile offshore like the top of a drowned skyscraper, a rampart missing and a stained-glass window shot through with holes just above the waterline. Its throne room has fallen. The hunters’ city sits in the north, the elves in the southeast.

Gehenna Bramble has spread out of the plains north of Zockau and over the city, and is rolling down the map toward the southeast, swallowing towns as it comes. Where it ends is the High Elf castle, sitting against a rocky bluff in the extreme southeast corner. Elle calls it the Sugar Cube: a white block 150 metres on a side in a clearing, with a thin open-topped tower at each corner, a drained moat and floors running underground into caves full of trolls. It is not stone. It is bleached wood, carved all over with acorns the size of a fingernail, and warm to the touch. There is a locked stairwell in its basement and two more in the woods nearby.

The castle is gone, carried off to the ninth floor, and the brambles have filled the whole world to within a hundred feet of the hole it left. Crawlers, hunters, elves and a swarm of mantis nymphs hang frozen in the air above the clearing in a rough cube. Then the brambles rise and close overhead into a dome, and the only light is a sickly yellow from the flower buds, pulsing to the music.

The NPCs who live here were crawlers once, says one of them, though some can no longer tell. The bush elves are the forest’s regular joes, almost indistinguishable from the high elves who rule them and a little bowed by it. Dryads, the walking tree people, share the villages with them, monkeys riding in their branches. The smaller settlements are guarded by Funeral Bells: eight-foot mushroom men in black robes at level 95, on duty day and night and with no sense of humour.

Bush elves, dryads and their monkeys live in the jungle villages behind Funeral Bell guards. The high elves rule the jungle from their city in the southeast; they are powerful magic users and attack everyone, and even the hunters keep away. Naiads live in the river and are as bad as the elves. Zockau is guarded by tall, muscled bears in heavy armour, and its pubs are full of hunters, aliens of every kind, drinking and waiting to be let out. One of them has already killed its mayor.

South of the river the towns belong to the ursine, big bear-like humanoids, and the bugbears, who are the commonest race in the Kapok district after the ursine and the bush elves. Point Mongo is an elderly ursine town that used to ban almost everything: dancing, swearing, naiads, macaques without a dryad, and dinosaurs of any kind; bugbears had to bathe in the river before entering. Its mayor is Donut now. Out in the jungle hunts Kiwi, head of a pack of clever, vicious Mongoliensis. Across the river the high elves rule, and the naiads hold the water.

The ursine hold Point Mongo, now Donut’s town, and the bugbears and bush elves the villages around it; Kiwi’s pack of Mongoliensis roams the jungle. Tsarina Signet, half naiad and half high elf, has come home with an army of bush elves and were-castors to take back her mother’s kingdom. The Naiad Confederacy that overthrew it is holed up in Fort Freedom, the old river palace. The high elves still rule the southeast. The hunters have organised into outfits and split the map between them: the Hive, the Dream, the Skull Empire, the Crafters, the Nebular Sin Patrol and others.

Fort Freedom has fallen to Signet’s army, and the naiads who held it are floating in the river. The ursine hold Point Mongo, the bugbears and bush elves their villages, and Kiwi’s raptors the jungle around them. Something has been attacking Point Mongo and the other towns: Big Tina, an allosaurus who wears a pink boa. The hunters still divide the map between their outfits, and the high elves still rule the southeast.

The High Elf castle is staffed by several kinds of elf: friendly level-40 Castle Guards in gold, white-clad soldiers, and black-and-gold, ninja-like elves who guard Queen Imogen herself. The caves in the rock under the castle are full of trolls, forever fighting the elves. Across the rest of the map the brambles are overrunning the towns, and the hunters who are left are scattered.

The hunters are not loose yet, but their minions and traps are, and some of them have been here for weeks. A hunter’s pet can be a pack of invisible Night Weasels that paralyse a level-95 guard without being seen. Stay on the trail if you go into the jungle. And do not make a Funeral Bell angry.

Zockau: every hunter on the floor is in it, the guards attack crawlers on sight, and when the grace period ends they spread out of it in every direction. The high elves attack anyone who comes near the southeast. The naiads in the river are just as bad, so stay out of the water. Hunters’ traps and pets are already waiting in the jungle, including invisible Night Weasels.

Hunters, more than a thousand of them at level 50 and up, hunting in outfits across territories they have carved up, with traps of their own; the elves of the Dream have built a trebuchet in the woods and are shelling Point Mongo with poison. The river holds naiads, fast enough to snatch a body off the bank. When it rains hard the confederates come up out of it. Dinosaurs probe the towns. In the southwest the hot springs were turned up and cooked a crowd of crawlers in the water, and the lava tubes there are now active. The high elves still attack everyone.

Vampirism has been spreading through the dinosaurs and the forest animals, and its source is gone now, which has cured thousands. What it left behind is worse. Fifty Odious Creepers, built from the leftovers of the slaughter and commandeered, Mordecai thinks, by a plant, are growing at random across the forest among a few thousand Shambling Berserkers, and every one is marked on the map. They are slow by day; in the dark they merge with each other and with the Shamblers, grow fast and copy themselves. It is a world quest for crawlers and hunters alike: kill all fifty before sunset, or something batshit happens to everyone. Hunters, the river and the elves remain.

The quest failed, and the punishment is Gehenna Bramble. Starting from the last two Odious Creepers, in the plains north of Zockau, every plant it touches becomes a ten-metre wall of thorned vines that thrashes and attacks; one prick and your blood boils away and you explode. It spreads at about four and a half kilometres an hour, faster at night, and cannot be countered or poisoned, only beaten back. It takes towns and buildings and everything but saferooms, and stops five metres short of a stairwell. Saferooms themselves now run on a blood bar that only killing fills. The hunters, the river and the elves are all still here.

Cage fight Extreme, four teams in and one out: the top crawlers, the last seventy-five hunters, Queen Imogen, a level 145 country boss with her elite guard, and Diwata, a level 250 god who cannot be killed. They fall together out of the air into a swarm of mantis nymphs, under a dome of brambles that has closed over the clearing.

layers.label: Carl and Donut, at Point Mongo

floors.name: The Great Race
floors.premise: Floor seven! A brand-new race, bought and paid for by our generous new partners: glass tunnels, pit stops, and a finish line full of portals. Several hundred kilometres of it. No dead ends, no going back. On your marks.

recap.title: Ten minutes
recap.text: The Great Race was a replacement, thrown together at the last minute with the Valtay's money for a slot whose original floor had been scrapped: a sealed circuit of glass tunnels with pit-stop safe rooms at the nodes, hundreds of kilometres long. Donut arrives in a fish tank, ranked number one, and picks a new class alone because the chat is down. She takes Viper Queen, which spits poison. Prepotente arrives in the pole-position chamber he bought with hunter hands at the Masquerade. Borant throws everything it has at him (freeze, paralysis, an administrative hold, four gnolls with guns), and the AI negates every piece of it and makes Borant follow its own rules. His mother's boots carried a fairy tale in their description, about a boy trapped in a maze whose tunnels seal behind him, who spends years learning how to crack the walls. The Apothecary had sent Donut a hammer and a metal rod, each marked with a small seven. Minutes after the floor opens, Prepotente brings the whole circuit down into fine dust. No crawler runs the maze. No mob, NPC or boss is ever met on it. Mordecai spends the ten minutes the seventh floor exists as a slime with no arms. The only floor of the crawl that was never played goes straight to the eighth, and the audience that paid for it in advance gets no refund.

floors.previously: On the Hunting Grounds: Carl blew up the hunters' city on the first night, wore the Ring of Divine Suffering like a personality, and gave a mantis gonorrhea. Miriam Dom waited for the sun. Beatrice turned up alive and drugged on a talk show, and Donut told her she was not her person any more. At the Butcher's Masquerade, Signet cut her own throat to break a goddess's seal, a whole castle went down a floor with the changelings in it, and Katia killed Eva and got a crown for her trouble. Only one of her and Donut can leave the ninth floor now. Next up: a race.

steps.text: The seventh floor is a race, finished just in time with the Valtay Corporation's money for a slot whose original design has been pushed down to the eighth. Twenty days sit on the collapse clock. Every crawler arrives sealed in a glass pod, and chat and magic stay off until the start. When the rules end, each pod slides in its turn to a starting chute and opens, and its crawler is pulled down a tube into the maze: several hundred kilometres of twisting glass tunnel, running from node to node, some nodes with hundreds of branches. All paths lead to the exit. There are no dead ends, and there is no backtracking. Each branch is marked with its danger and its distance, and some ask for a puzzle or a sum before they let anyone through. Pitstop saferooms sit in the nodes. Most major nodes have a zero tube with no danger in it, and a zero tube can be passed only once; any other path closes for a while once ten crawlers or a single party have been through. The exits are stairwell portals, and they pull from the first second. A boon bought on the floor above puts its buyer's party at the very front. The floor is built on a fairy tale, the Great Race, and built like a Prince Rupert's drop: crack it in the right place and the whole level goes.

The seventh floor is open for ten minutes. It was a race through several hundred kilometres of glass tunnel, pod by pod down a starting chute, node to node with no dead ends and no backtracking, every branch marked with its danger, and a zero tube at most major nodes for whoever reached it first. It was built to follow its fairy tale exactly, and the boy in the tale breaks the maze the same way the goat does; it only took him thousands of years. Mordecai puts it on the engineers. A level doomed by its own design is not new, but none has failed this fast. The Syndicate pays for the livestream in advance, and a floor that is skipped is not refunded. Nor does the floor's spellbook delivery: Donut's mailbox has nothing from the seventh floor in it.

The race starts in a pole-position chamber: a featureless room of clear glass no bigger than a living room. Three of its walls are solid. The fourth is a row of thick glass bars, like a jail cell, with a timer over them, and past the bars a round tunnel curves downward into the dark like a waterslide. The floor is as slick as ice, and a gentle tug draws everything toward the bars. The pods are stacked in a corkscrew, each one a step of a spiral staircase climbing into the dark, and the bottom step goes first. Up the hollow middle of the spiral runs a wide glowing tube of exits: stairwells to the eighth floor with no stairs and no doors, round portals stacked one above another like a string of beads, bright enough to hurt. Somewhere past the chutes lies the maze itself, which nobody sees. A few minutes after the floor opens, all of it, pods, chutes and tunnels, explodes into a fine dust.

The only occupants are crawlers, each party in its own fish tank on the spiral, with more pods visible through the glass above and to one side. In one near the edge of sight Donut thinks she sees Agatha; Carl can only make out a shopping cart. The lowest pod, the pole position, holds Carl, Donut and Prepotente, who bought it with hunter hands at the Masquerade and leaves the party once he is in it, so that Donut leads. He knows the fairy tale from his mother's boots, whose description tells the whole of it. The rules are read by Cascadia, the woman who gives the daily updates, far too fast. Borant has no one on the floor, though it tries to put four gnolls with guns into the pole-position chamber, and they are gone in a crackle of smoke.

Crawlers are the only occupants, each party in its own glass pod on the spiral; Donut thinks one of the far ones holds Agatha's shopping cart. Carl, Donut and Prepotente share the pole position, and Prepotente, who knows the fairy tale from his mother's boots, is the one who breaks the floor. Cascadia reads the rules, and the floor is hers: she worked hard to make it happen. Borant sends four armed gnolls that never arrive. Guides do not come through untouched. For the ten minutes the floor is open, Mordecai is a slime with no arms.

Out in the maze the course is the killer. Some paths are much more dangerous than others, and a path once taken cannot be backed out of. The safe zero tubes go to whoever gets there first, and the announcement has a warning for those at the back that it never finishes. In the pole-position chamber the danger is the showrunners. Borant throws peace bonding, a freeze, paralysis, a slow, a teleport and an administrative hold at the three crawlers inside, one after another for fifteen seconds, and the AI negates every one of them. Then the glass itself. The Enchanted Stick of Cascadia's Screams goes halfway into the back wall, one tiny tap of the Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward sends a lightning pattern of cracks across it, and the whole level shatters. Every crawler on the floor is sucked into the stairwells at once, tumbling head over toes, and arrives covered in glass dust. Donut coughs up glass shards. Donut also loses health to her own choice: with the chat down she takes a new class alone, Viper Queen, which shoots poison blobs.

floors.name: The Ghosts of Earth
floors.premise: Welcome to the eighth floor! It's your own planet, a few weeks before I arrived. Everybody's here, going about their business, and none of them know. Look, don't touch: anything you take from them turns to dust when the floor goes. Oh, and it's a card game now. Every monster down here was somebody's folk tale. Catch them, deal them, lose them.
