recap.title: Havana, before
recap.text: Donut picks Cuba over the Bahamas book Carl bought, and they come up inside Havana's capitol on December 10th, before the collapse. The whole floor is a replay of the world weeks before it ended, full of memory ghosts who walk through you, and every monster is a local legend. Each squad gets twenty flags: plant one in a monster below five per cent and it becomes a T'Ghee card, a totem you can summon. Fill six slots in fourteen days. Mordecai is a pink hills cyclops, and finally tells the story behind his hatred. On his own tenth floor his brother Uzzi died because Odette refused to pay the sponsor of a storm goddess, and had Chaco put a god-summoning dart into Uzzi instead of letting Mordecai sacrifice himself. For killing every hunter on the last floor Carl gets a Celestial box, and from it the Scavenger's Daughter, a divine jacket patch that eats souls. Donut becomes a Master Telephone Psychic whose best spell makes monsters stab themselves. Their first monster is a wolf with Che Guevara's head. Their first allies are three Cubans, Paz, his cousin Anton and a cat-girl nun called Sister Ines, who arrive hostile because of something Donut once said about cat girls to a stripper. Together they flag a kung-fu monk seal called Geraldo and stumble into the Chowder War, crabs against seals. The pacifist network asks, through Zev, for Carl to go on a show called Shadow Boxer.

recap.title: Shadow Boxer
recap.text: The card rules arrive at length: a squad leader in deck combat loses spells and inventory until the deck is spent, and the squad has to keep them alive. Samantha writes from inside a spider demigoddess in the southern swamps, a woman of many names, one of them the Bedlam Bride, who says she is looking for her husband. In the practice arena Donut's four cards float in front of her face like a windshield, and Geraldo arrives flipping, in a headband covered in hearts. A cemetery hides a corrupted town, and Paz's Santero class wakes the dead. A dying orisha called Asojano, Lord of Smallpox, follows them into the saferoom and asks Paz to repair his shrine. Donut's fans vote her a golden headset that finally lets her sing in tune. Then Shadow Boxer, whose host is Rosetta Thagra, a former crawler whose note Carl has read in the Cookbook's bomb chapter. She interviews Donut about Gossip Girl. She asks Carl about his mother, and Donut learns for the first time that his mother hanged herself and that he found her. Rosetta shows him a faked photograph with a jug of milk in it and asks about potatoes, and the room blinks. Harbinger, the caprid liaison who once helped Maggie My, stops the interview and bans her for talking in code. Quasar brings news of the ninth floor: the high elf castle came down on the Lemig Sortion's army and splattered half of it.

recap.title: Seven shrines
recap.text: Carl rolls troll-smoke bombs down the street and Bomo carries the terrified Paz across a graveyard to Asojano's temple. Inside is a thorn room with seven broken shrines and enough power to fix one. Gods appear from every side to argue their case. Paz and Anton's own god, Ogun, demands they choose his, and Katia messages Carl alone: fix Yemaya's, because it is the first step towards getting the Crown of the Sepsis Whore off her head. Anton, charmed, throws Ogun's piece out of the door. Bomo builds Yemaya's shrine like Tetris, Donut and Mongo take Asojano apart, and Carl flags him a heartbeat before he dies. Ogun comes for his worshippers. He burns an unhealable handprint into Paz's face and crushes Anton's head underfoot while Carl tries to shield him. Dying, Paz tells them what Sister Ines is: a cat girl whose race makes everyone near her protect her, and before the crawl the Reaper of Havana, who poisoned every sister in her convent. Paz asks to be let go, and she stabs a flag into his neck and turns him into a card. Yemaya rises, sends Bomo off to join the Sledge, and brings Eileithyia, a goddess driven by Huanxin Jinx, the sponsor whose price Odette refused on Mordecai's tenth floor. In secret Eileithyia offers Carl a deal: accept Odette as adjutant, and she will fix the votes and the crown. Katia's way out is a flower in a sealed box. Eating it grants one of Eileithyia's boons: become a celestial attendant on the twelfth floor, or become pregnant and leave the crawl. The last seal is a contract from the Night Wyrm's guild: kill Astrid.

recap.title: The planning table
recap.text: Mordecai has quietly hired the sickest of the changeling children as his room attendants and set up a split controller on the floor for Ruby, who has no arms. The ninth floor's warlords meet virtually around a table: an orc prince, a naga, a blob, a surfer goblin called Luke, Empress D'nadia, a robot, a masked Viceroy. The Viceroy's head comes off mid-sentence. Juice Box is sitting in his chair wearing Epitome's mother's face, and since she is an NPC on nobody's team, the rules cannot touch her. Her price for stopping is a tenth team, made of the floor's own NPCs, with the same protections as the nine. Carl files it as an action item, and within minutes Prince Stalwart takes a magical arrow through the eye. Florin hands Donut the card of Uzi Jesus, a zombie gunman who once shot him. In the Penis Parade, the strip club off the top floor of the Desperado Club, a dancer called Damascus Steel walks Carl through the back of a cubicle to the Guild of Suffering. A voice in the dark gives him a map of the club's secret passages. They flag Raul, a meditating land crab who calls himself worthless, by dropping him through the floor of a box truck. Then they reach Samantha and her new friend Shi Maria, the Bedlam Bride. Carl sees through the spider's act and makes a deal: she becomes a card in their deck, and they carry her to the next floor.

recap.title: Astrid
recap.text: Phases two and three are announced. Each squad leader is sent somewhere new to fetch a stairwell key, and squads without one are thrown against the squads that have one. Katia is out of it on a drug from a hidden bar in the club, reliving her baby daughter, and Imani and Mordecai start her cure. Empress D'nadia sells her sponsorship of Donut to a garbage-hauling company. In practice fights Shi Maria opens her fifth eye and something tugs at the river in the back of Carl's mind. Carl insists on the assassination anyway. He lays teleport traps in the service corridor Astrid uses and walls off a door marked with a warning. Samantha's distraction goes too far, into the casino, and pulls Minge, a feral demon and Slit's little sister, out of a door into the Nothing. Astrid is braver than anyone expected: she releases the vorpals, god-deputised suicide troops, to kill the demon. In the club kitchen Katia's totems pin her, Carl pulls her wings off, and a spike goes through her head. Before she dies she asks Carl to tell her husband she did it to keep them safe. Her husband is Hamed, the Night Wyrm, the demigod who ordered the killing. Two dancers are crying on the floor of the Penis Parade: Damascus Steel and Anaconda, her sons. Astrid and the Night Wyrm were crawlers once, long ago, and never left. Damascus makes Carl hire every male dancer in the club as mercenaries with his coupon before the restructuring comes, then walks off with his brother to find their father. Katia has the orchid.

recap.title: The Keys
recap.text: On Odette's show Carl tells the galaxy that the faction officials who got flushed into the shark-filled ruins of Larracos should be thanking him. Odette shows D'nadia's rejected action items, one of which would have deleted Carl and Donut outright. Then she does not ask to be their adjutant. She has sponsored a goddess of her own, Nekhebit, and is going into the Ascendency herself, so the whole segment was a press conference. They pick Baroness Victory instead. In fifteen minutes off the record Odette tells Carl her real reason: every world the crawl is run on is burned for fuel, she means to shut it down, and the guilt over Uzzi drives everything she does. Eileithyia keeps the deal, and promises to crush everyone Carl loves if he ever warns Odette. Donut goes into the phase-two choosing room alone and terrified. She picks Miami, a glitch drops them in the Florida Keys, and the key sits on top of a chunk of Iowa that has been set down on the reef. The squads are scattered all over the world, and some of the key sites are cruel. Imani's is in her childhood home in Detroit. Katia's is Tran's family's apartment in Da Nang. They fight their way through nine deckmasters for tokens. Asojano and Uzi Jesus merge into a single totem called Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang. After one close fight Donut admits she is frightened and does not want to be in charge, and Carl reads someone on her feed threatening to stop watching because she is whiny. He turns the screen off, and they nap in a chair.

recap.title: Asher
recap.text: Jola, a house-sized Yule Cat Katia gave Donut, eats a Nightgaunt. In a barn full of turkeys a necromancer ogre pins Carl, pierced and blind, and whispers that they are starved, and that he could satiate them all. Raul breaks her staff and takes her head, and the Scavenger's Daughter obliterates a turkey god with a kick that tilts the barn off the mountain. Then the key-holder's trailer, which Donut does not want him to enter because she recognised the motorcycle outside. It is a single-wide in a summer yard spliced into December, with his father's Harley out front. Inside, a recording: his father, yellow and dying in a hospital bed, cursing the Mariners. A young wife in scrubs. And a six-year-old boy with Carl's nose. Asher. Carl has a brother, and learns it today. His stepmother fills a syringe with morphine and says yes, it is about time. Carl does not watch. He takes the Glock, the boy's crayon drawings and a Centipede cabinet, and sets fire to the drapes. The boss is the Reminiscence Hydra, nine heads wearing the faces of people from his life, among them Bea's mother and Asher, who fires lightning at him and asks why he never visited. Shi Maria bites the Asher head off to let it rest, and says Carl owes her something now; her fifth eye has done something to him. Afterwards Donut tells him Bea ran his Facebook, got a coworker fired for asking him out, and knew about Asher all along. Until today he was never angry at her.

recap.title: Residuals
recap.text: Louis insists on Christmas. On the recap Orren tells the galaxy that the AI has taken the controls from the showrunners and has settled most of them back in exchange for concessions. Every faction on the ninth floor tries to withdraw, and the AI refuses them all. Carl's pacifist network sends a crumpled flyer: a homeless shelter in Homestead, breakfast at seven. Zev warns him that the box was seized days ago and that everyone in the charity has vanished, Rosetta included. At the shelter a man in a red trapper hat gives the same speech he has given every morning for a year, in case a crawler ever stood there. He is Goff, a Residual, one of thousands waiting on Earth to teach the new AI something. Let me tell you how to shut off the, he begins, and Orren yanks Carl out, calling it a trap meant to trigger the failsafe. Agatha is a Residual too, of a different kind. Phase three. Only two squads in Cuba hold keys, Carl's and Sister Ines's. Imani's own totem killed her whole squad. She arrives in Cuba with no key and runs into a saferoom, and Quan Ch is waiting outside it. The Chowder War collapses into slaughter, Sister Ines charms a city boss serpent and an army of zombie seals and crabs, and so much dies at once that Sheol overflows. A Demon Eviction begins, sending demons up into every fresh corpse.

recap.title: Nobody gets left behind
recap.text: Quan Ch plays Force Play twice. Sister Ines and Donut both flee, and both keys go to him. He surfaces at the exit Tserendolgor's squad is holding, and Carl throws Samantha fifteen kilometres to deliver himself there. Jola strips Quan naked, a golden Uzi Jesus empties two guns into him, and dying he asks for the For Daddy ring back. Carl drops it in his hand. But the door is failing, Donut is kilometres away, and there is no time to hand a key across. Ren confesses to Donut that she cheated at the pet show, hands Carl her gear, and brings the building down on herself. The keys are Donut's. Then Carl and Prepotente work out a way to save everyone without one. A demon prince called Amayon, trapped in Ines's serpent, is casting a spell to go home that will suck every soul in its range upward. If crawlers tunnel under their stairwell chambers, it might tear the walls away and pull them up in. Everyone digs. Lucia's parting gift of Doggy Door upgrades brings Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Na's squads to the church, and Carl realises that what was breaking them all along was loneliness. Louis kills Sister Ines while she sleeps, and her patron goddess Ysalte arrives to claim the demon. Raul fertilises an ocean of crab eggs to refill the world with souls. Carl burns himself down to two per cent to unleash his Martyr's Path fire, and a warped Paz, summoned by the goddess herself, kills her with Katia's god-killing bolt. Amayon casts. Shi Maria takes Carl's body, tears out Li Jun's eye and eats it, then tattoos herself into Carl's chest. The viewers vote the sponsors' protections off by ninety-eight per cent and seat the tenth team, and Carl and Donut ride the stairwell down to the war, together. Above the planet, a garbage freighter carrying fifty thousand former crawlers requests clearance.

floors.previously: The seventh floor lasted about ten minutes, because a goat broke it. Don't ask. Before that, the Hunting Grounds: Carl blew up the hunters' city, gave a mantis gonorrhea, and watched Miriam Dom wait for the sun. Signet broke a goddess's peace seal with her own throat, a castle went down a floor with the changelings inside, and Katia killed Eva and inherited the Sepsis crown. Only one of her and Donut can leave the ninth floor. Oh, and Beatrice is alive. Now: your planet, as it was a few weeks before I arrived. Try not to get attached.

steps.text: The floor is Earth, or a recording of it: an exact copy of the planet's surface as it stood on December 10th, weeks before the collapse, cut into 293 regions with two stairwells apiece. Every crawler has been put into a squad of no more than five that cannot be broken, and every squad has six empty slots. For fourteen days each squad is held in its starting area, about 99 kilometres out from where it started in any direction, and no more than six kilometres offshore on an island. The people and animals of the recording are ghosts who walk straight through you. Everything else is solid and keeps its mass and momentum, and anything looted from the memory turns to dust when the floor collapses. The monsters come from the local folklore, and they get harder the further out you go. The squad leader carries twenty flags: plant one in a monster below five per cent health and it becomes a T'Ghee totem, a card that can be summoned. Fill the six slots before the timer runs out, or they are filled at random. The stairwell is right there, and it needs a key nobody can get until phase two.

Fights are card games now. A squad's deck needs six totems in it, plus as many utility, mystic, snare and special cards as the leader cares to carry. When combat starts four random cards are drawn, and each card played is replaced at one every ten seconds. A totem fights for the time printed on its card; knocked out, it is out for the rest of that fight. When the other side carries a deck too, deck-to-deck combat is forced, and the squad leader loses their own spells and their inventory until the deck is spent. Most totems cannot touch the opposing leader while enemy totems still stand, so the rest of the squad keeps its leader alive. Kill a squad and its cards are yours. Every saferoom now has a practice arena, for a fee. Underneath, the floor is unchanged: a recording of Earth full of ghosts, folklore monsters, twenty flags and a locked stairwell.

The rest of the floor has been laid out. At 12:01 on December 24th every squad is pulled into a room like the one it started in, and the leader gets at least two places to choose between and sixty seconds to choose. Every totem not in the active deck is lost, and from then on a squad holds exactly six. The new place is another memory, populated by intelligent mobs who carry decks of their own. A key is marked on the map ten to fifteen kilometres away, and there are 48 hours to reach it. It opens only the stairwell beside the squad's own starting area, and only the keyholder's squad may pass. At midnight on December 26th phase three begins: keyholders are sent back home, and squads without a key are sent to stand in the doorway of someone who has one. Kill them before they leave, and the key is yours.

Phase two is running. The squads have been scattered to new regions of the same recording, each with six totems and nothing spare, and 46 hours left on the key. The route to the key is guarded by deckmasters, intelligent mobs with decks who stand frozen along the path until a squad comes close, so every one of them is a card fight. Beat one and its cards hang in the air for the taking, though taking one of its totems means giving up one of your own. The key opens one door only, the stairwell beside the squad's starting area, and only for the keyholder's squad.

Phase three. It is December 26th, the stairwell locations are open, and a key is the only way through the door: only the keyholder's squad may pass, and the key dissipates when it is used. Every keyholder has been dropped back into their home region, somewhere within reach of the exit, with four days and seventeen hours left before the floor collapses. In the Cuba zone there are five squads, and two of them hold keys. The other three have nowhere to go but the doorways of the two that do.

Sheol is overflowing. So much has died at once that a Demon Eviction has begun across Cuba: demons are being flung up out of the underworld and into anything recently fallen or weakened, and a zombie is the easiest shell of all. The bigger the battle, the bigger the possession. A demon that wants to go home can only do it by dragging another soul down with it. Underneath, the floor still runs as before: two keys in the zone, five squads, and a door at each stairwell that opens only for a keyholder.

The squad arrives in El Capitolio Nacional de Cuba, the old capitol building in downtown Havana, in a long, empty hall of marble and tile. Blue and magenta tiles run off in both directions, tall arched windows line the walls, and a half-pipe ceiling of bronze squares rises to a cupola in the middle. Street lamps hung with Christmas ribbon light it yellow. The doors are locked. At the end of the hall is a door to the stairwell, and it needs a key. Outside the windows there is nothing yet but swirling black smoke.

Outside it is a warm, humid December morning in Havana. A long stone stairway runs down from the capitol to a wide sidewalk and a busy two-lane road, and beyond it the city packs in tight: Spanish colonial buildings of brick and old, many-coloured stucco, several storeys high, with palm-filled parks between them. The streets are full of Chinese and Russian cars, scooters, buses and classic American cars from the fifties. A multi-lane highway runs along the northern coast with the ocean on the other side, and past Old Havana lies a neighbourhood called Miramar. Wherever a car has hit something, a pile-up is starting to grow.

Havana runs from the capitol out to the coast highway, the ocean along its northern edge and car pile-ups growing at every crash. Inside the city is the Colón Cemetery, several blocks wide, behind its old concrete archway. The recording has put a towering black, spiked fence around it, and inside the fog is a corrupted town, a ghommid settlement with a Club Vanquisher spire in its square. A paved street runs through the graveyard to the octagonal yellow church at its centre, La Iglesia de los Olvidados, with its door hanging by one hinge, moss on the tiles and a hole in the roof. Inside are seven broken shrines.

Phase two has put Carl and Donut in Monroe County, Florida: the Keys, at the very bottom of the map, a bigger area than they had in Cuba. It is a narrow beach town on a two-lane road under sparse streetlamps, the cars already gone. To the west stands something that does not belong. A sheer wall of crumbling earth has been upended over the island, wider than the island itself and climbing into the clouds, and the key is up there somewhere. It is a piece of Iowa, ripped out of the ground around the key and set down on a cay built on a reef, and the sea is already eating at its base.

The top of the mound is Dallas County, Iowa, set down above the Florida Keys with the ocean visible on either side. Its edges are wet asphalt that breaks away underfoot. Up there are a street of farm-style houses, a sparse trailer park and half of a commercial farm, its buildings and a silo standing close to the edge, and a long corrugated turkey barn like an aircraft hangar. The snow that came with it has melted, and the whole place is mud, sliding a few feet at a time into the sea.

Phase three has brought the keyholders home, and Havana is burning. Smoke rises from all over the city and many of its buildings are on fire. The capitol, where the floor began, is a battleground, its front door blown out and glass down the steps, and the zone's other stairwell is inside a church across town. Several miles to the west a gout of flame is rising into the sky.

Everybody lives here, and none of them are here. The planet's whole population is going about December 10th as it was recorded, tourists and drivers and vendors and street dogs, and none of them can see a crawler or show up on a map. Touch one and you pass straight through, and their clothes stay behind. What actually lives here is the local folklore: Romania has vampires and werewolves, Ireland has leprechauns and banshees, and every region gets its own.

Havana's ghosts go about their day, and its monsters come out of Cuban legend as the dungeon misremembers it, like the Experience, a wolf-sized guardian of the dead with a bearded man's head in a red beret. Along the coast a war is brewing. The Monk Seals, kung-fu sentries who hold the ocean sacred, are set against the Red Maníseros Land Crabs, who have to reach that ocean every year to spawn. Geraldo, a monk seal, already fights for Carl and Donut. Three other crawlers share Havana and came up at its other stairwell: Paz Lo, a Santero in silver plate; his cousin Anton, a tattooed fugitive with a crossbow; and Sister Ines, a cat-girl nun the two of them guard closely.

Inside the Colón Cemetery lives a whole town of ghommids, visitors from the land of the dead, no two of them alike: a man made of mouths, toddler-sized minotaurs, a donkey-headed thing. The settlement has been corrupted, and its people are a slow, freezing, wailing horde that the dark makes worse. Behind it is Asojano, the Lord of Smallpox, an orisha and a level-130 city boss, a dying spirit who wants his shrine in the church at the centre repaired. Out on the coast the seals and crabs are still squaring up. Paz, Anton and Sister Ines are travelling with Carl and Donut.

Asojano is gone, and the ghommid village is cured: the fog has lifted and the creatures turn and wave as crawlers pass, as if it were a cartoon. Havana's other crawlers are scattered. Anton is dead under a god's foot. Paz is a card. Sister Ines is out there alone, and she is what the papers once called the Reaper of Havana. Out on the coast the Chowder War between the seals and the crabs is still building.

The Keys are full of memory ghosts on an empty road, and of something new: intelligent mobs with decks of their own, waiting one by one along the path to the key. Babababoons, a Reef Explorer in a glowing deep-dive suit, Swordfish Interlopers that spit water and launch themselves into the sky. On the Iowa ground at the top there is a Nightgaunt on a farmhouse roof, a barn full of live turkeys, and a necromancer ogre who has been raising them into zombie turkeys.

Five squads are left in the Cuba zone, two of them holding keys. Imani is here too, alone, with no key, after her own totem killed her squad, and she has run into a saferoom inside a church. Quan Ch is outside it, also alone.

The world itself. The people are ghosts, but their cars, buses and buildings are solid, and a passing car can kill a crawler. The further out from the start, the harder the monsters and bosses. The monsters are hunting the ghosts too, so the dumb ones are easy to spot. And the clock: fourteen days to fill six slots, or the squad is filled at random. Those in Japan are just plain fucked.

Traffic. One crash in a road brings every car behind it into the same pile, and the piles grow longer than anyone expects until the roads are stopped, and moving things are hitting crawlers harder than they should. Folklore monsters wait in the parks, the Experience among them, a magical guardian of the dead that charges barking. Seals haunt the shoreline, and further out something like a sea serpent breaks the surface.

The Colón Cemetery. Its fence cannot be seen through, its streets are fog, and the corrupted ghommid town inside is a horde of thousands, slow but relentless. Touching one with bare skin freezes you, and at night they glow blue and wail. Its city boss carries a disease that comes off him. In the streets outside, the car piles and the fires keep growing, and the folklore monsters keep hunting.

Southwest of Havana, past the car piles, the land flattens into trees, wetland and a nature preserve near the southern coast, and the crab migration crosses the road there: tens of thousands of Red Maníseros Land Crabs, level seventy and up, swarming for the sea. Further on, white web fills the woods beside the road, sticky to a single strand, strewn with crab husks and bones. It belongs to Shi Maria, a spider as dangerous as anything the crawl has offered.

Every fight is a card fight with a deckmaster, and the squad leader goes into each one with no spells and no inventory until the deck runs out. The mound of Iowa is coming apart under its own weight, the sea eating at the base and the meltwater at the top, and whole buildings are falling off the edge. On top, a Nightgaunt hides on a roof, and the barn holds the boss: zombie turkeys and the ones who raise them. Turkeys that fall off the edge land in the ocean.

Everything at once. The zombism that started in Iowa's farm animals is in the sea now, so the fish, the seals and the crabs are rising again, and the Demon Eviction is putting demons into them that want to drag you down into Sheol. The Madre de Aguas, a level-125 sea-snake city boss, has died of the curse and risen again, and a demon prince called Amayon has slipped into her. Hell has come to burn the world, starting with Havana. And at each stairwell, squads without a key are waiting for the ones who have one.

layers.label: A giant snake on the shore

floors.name: Faction Wars
floors.premise: Welcome to Faction Wars, the main event! Nine armies camped around a city, a castle at the bottom of it, and thirty days to take it. You're soldiers now. Pick a side, or get drafted by one. Oh, and one teensy rule change this season: nobody respawns. Not you. Not them. Enjoy the war.

recap.title: Larracos
recap.text: They come down into Larracos at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire. Nine armies ring the drowned city like slices of a pie, the city's own NPCs defend it as the tenth team, and whoever takes the castle at the bottom of the well wins. Carl and Donut are warlords of one of the nine, the Princess Posse. Carl carries a secret from Christmas morning. The Residual's coffee held an illegal implant, a Containment Interface, that can trip the failsafe and turn the sun nova. Donut becomes a Deathbed Hellcat, a long-range sniper who comes with a ghillie suit. Elle is a Hailstorm Queen. Mordecai is a human Canadian in a raccoon hat with his best alchemy table yet. Carl drinks a Hell-Kissed potion that lets him turn briefly incorporeal and pass through things. He adopts Tserendolgor's baby tummy acher and names it Sir Rendlegore, which Donut takes as a betrayal. Katia's hair tonic gives him hair to his waist. Louis's celestial box brings him a war airship called the Party Planner. Juice Box has woken Larracos's NPCs to what they are, calls herself Warlord, and wants to seal the alliance by marrying Louis. Ferdinand, mayor of the shantytown outside the walls, holds her team's warlord interface, and Carl trades him back his hat and his rhinoceros for the mayoralty. The Desperado Club reopens under new management: Hamed, the Night Wyrm. The Dream has bought Signet's old show, Vengeance of the Daughter, and wants its third season.

recap.title: Fifty thousand
recap.text: At the Posse's headquarters Carl finds Rosetta, a former crawler called Tipid, a skyfowl called Justice Light, and fifty thousand former crawlers who came down in the garbage freighter to fight for him. Tipid explains that Doctor Hu, who wrote the Cookbook's second edition, gathered them. Carl cries. The castle is called the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, and Donut forbids anyone to read out the initials. An elite sent by the company behind Signet's old show walks in wearing satchel charges, and Baroness Victory, their adjutant, cuts him down. Carl's spam folder shows Shi Maria trying to cast through him, blocked by a toe ring he has barely noticed. Mordecai brews Glory Bound. For Katia, a trip into her worst memory to cure the drugs. For Carl, a trip into the spider's worst memory, to lock her inside it. They hold hands going under, and their dreams bleed together: a children's hospital in Iceland, and Annie. Inside the dream Shi Maria's husband Hapanzi seals her in Carl like an egg only Carl can break. Meanwhile the Lemig Sortion and the Madness cheat. They time a Summon Ally spell with outside knowledge to pull Carl's sleeping body into their base and let the spider loose on the Posse. Carl wakes in the Lemig headquarters, standing in a circle of fifty dead goblins. At the hearing, the adjutants replay Katia's dream for everyone. The Lemig commander looks into the eye on Carl's chest, goes mad and kills himself. The ceasefire ends early, and the Madness's Architect Houston shoots Carl through the shoulder as he teleports home.

recap.title: Over the top
recap.text: In flashback: on Christmas morning, beside a sleeping memory dog, Carl opened the containment interface, found the button that would destroy everything, and pressed the one beside it instead. Disconnect Containment. The failsafe is dead, and the AI's sphere begins to grow. Now the war starts. On the southern front the Posse holds against the Dream, the Prism Kingdom and the nagas, then against a swarm of the Reavers' plague-carrying pets. Carl orders enemies taken alive where possible. Then they go on the attack. Louis's bombs make craters in no man's land, fifty trap speakers blast Killing in the Name, and two thousand invisible soldiers go over the top. In the craters they read Build Trench scrolls to dig straight into the enemy lines, a craft-magic exploit nobody ever fixed. Carl lands on a Saccathian soldier with the Daughter's Kiss, blows their trench apart and knocks himself out for twenty-five seconds. They take the Prism castle. Carl puts the Ring of Divine Suffering's mark on Empress D'nadia and finds himself standing on an edge, wanting to kill her with his own hands more than he has wanted anything. He steps back. Donut tells the Empress that Mongo would like to express his disappointment at how she judged the pet show, and Mongo kills her. Carl's stats now make him party leader of the Royal Court. Donut begs him to throw the ring away because it is changing him. Not yet, he says.

recap.title: The king's daughter
recap.text: Agatha turns up in the shantytown asking for Carl by name, and the Syndicate's prime minister sends word to stay away from her. The Reavers come through the Posse's own saferoom door, and Valtay worms have taken over the Posse's mages, so the fortress fills with enemies from inside. Carl punches one worm out of a dead man's face, and Donut stands on the roof shouting Comrades and sets Big Tina loose. Then the Skull Empire's army arrives under King Rust, the Maestro's father, and asks to parley. The king is crying. His daughter, Princess Formidable, has taken one of his warships and told the Syndicate she will trip the failsafe herself to keep the rogue AI away from the centre of the galaxy. He wants Carl to beg her to stop for the sake of Earth's people. Carl laughs, trades a truce for a withdrawal, and privately tells Donut not to worry, because it won't work. He knows the failsafe is dead because he killed it. On the walk back Rosetta kills the king, uses his ring and his eye on a data pad, and empties his accounts. His army attacks. At the same moment a former crawler called Volteeg, commanding a Weeper for the Operatic Collective, detonates it, killing ten thousand soldiers and his own warlord. The Operatic Collective is out of the war. Carl, Donut and Rosetta fall into a tunnel the Semeru dwarves dug under the field.

recap.title: A drink with the AI
recap.text: Orren pulls Carl into his office. His people know about Paulie and the implant, and they cannot work out how it functions. Then Growler Gary walks in, except it is the AI wearing him, drinking vodka and unhappy with Orren for trying to have Carl killed. It teleports Princess Formidable into the room to show everyone that the button she pressed did nothing, then drops her on Earth. It asks their advice, in a long metaphor about a boyfriend in prison, on whether to side with Agatha's Residuals or the Apothecary. Donut tells it to stay out of it until it knows whether the boyfriend is good or bad. The Bloc of enemy teams starts to break up. Katia tattoos Carl with one of Li Na's spells in ink made from the pacifist network's root vegetable. Zev reports that when Formidable's crew hit the button, a whole other star system went dark. At the warlord council Stalwart punches the commentator, a system message announces that Scolopendra stirs, and Juice Box turns into something she calls one of the Unwashed and tells the galaxy it is coming for them all. Then Odette mentions that the Blood Sultanate owns the company that made Blood Hunter, the show that killed Miriam Dom. Carl starts laughing and cannot stop. The nagas have so few troops because most of their army is already dead.

recap.title: Operation Snake Pit
recap.text: Donut cannot leave this floor until every royal of the Blood Sultanate is dead, and Katia, crowned by Eva, is bound the same way. Operation Snake Pit was supposed to take care of it. Prepotente, level 99, got there first: most of the naga army is already dead at his hooves, revenge for Miriam. He lands, says recruit me, and sobs that Carl is his best friend. Carl makes him a colonel. Elle and Imani kill a royal inside the naga castle. Their sultana, Vinata, has been escaping death every season by slipping into Club Vanquisher and a god's temple. So Carl, Katia, Prepotente and Samantha break into the club, with a wire carrying Li Na's dread auras ahead of them that turns the guards against themselves in horrible ways. Samantha opens the door to the temple of Khepri, and it is a trap with a god inside. The Scavenger's Daughter gives Carl ninety seconds of immortality in a god's presence. He summons a fat one-hit creature called Günter and sets off a bomb at his own feet in a narrow room, and survives being turned inside out. Everything else dies except the god and Vinata. Gods spill out into the club. Hellik steps out to banish Khepri and gives Carl a message for Emberus: Hellik did not kill his son, Apito has been corrupted, and Nekhebit is behind it. Carl's disease ring overloads, the slugpox comes back, and a sluggalette called Bigs kills Vinata the second her immortality runs out. In a hidden guild Carl finds Milk, who wrote in the Cookbook, and holds her while he cries.

recap.title: Operation Ruin
recap.text: The Posse builds the Nest, a granite tower that Donut wants painted purple, designed to draw every long-range spell on the battlefield while she snipes from the top. Their captive naga, Rishi, tells Carl a Syndicate court has named him the de facto leader of Earth, and offers Earth's natives citizenship if the nagas can settle the rest of the solar system. Carl marks him and kills him. Then Operation Ruin: four offensives at once. Florin takes the orcs, Boomer the Reavers, Donut the Dream from the Nest, and Carl the Madness. Louis flies bombing runs with Carl aboard to make the bombs bigger. Elle opens the Gate of the Feral Gods, and out come Meatus, a gremlin wearing a god's stolen penis, and Harpocrates, the god of silence, who wants it back. The Semeru set off the mountain under King's Point, the orcs' castle, next door to Reaver territory. Someone summons Eris, goddess of chaos, and a demon eviction begins. Then Prince Stalwart teleports in with Akuma, leader of a war mage rebellion, and explodes. Akuma takes the Gate and vanishes. Carl realises everyone keeps making plans around him without telling him. A dragon appears over the Reaver castle, Yarilo comes out of the Gate chasing Samantha, and in the Madness territory Osvaldo, who belongs to no army, holds up Apito's memorial crystal, which blazes into a rainbow the size of a hill and brings the whole Madness down on Carl's group.

recap.title: The ball of everyone
recap.text: The Viceroys of the Madness pour psionics into Carl. A friendly voice tells him to look at his feet. They are buried in the root of an All Tree, and his Mind Balance jumps to sixteen as the tree dies behind him. Then Eris casts the Ceremony of Chaos. Everyone but Carl, the sluggalos and the strippers freezes, and she piles them all, friends and enemies, into a heap beside the Dream castle, conscious and invulnerable. The Party Planner is torn open and Louis falls into the Reaver castle. Donut commits an atrocity. With a stolen spell from a skunk's hat and her tower behind it, she rolls the pile into one enormous ball and drives it like a remote-control car. Meatus pulls Eris into it with him. When Harpocrates chases it, she plays Lollipop at him over the PA. Carl and a stripper named Dong break into the Madness castle, with Dong's sapient sock-flail advising them. They find Architect Houston grafting himself onto a changeling on his own surgical table, with a captive crawler, Burcu, tongueless and chained beside him. Carl phases through Houston and kills him. Burcu dies in the traps. Across the field Harpocrates marks Donut for death, and Li Jun throws himself in the way, and it costs him his life. The Madness is defeated, the Peeling phase opens Larracos to attack, and the war mages, recognised as a team at last under a warlord named Agatha, occupy the castle. Donut drives the ball onto a field of corpses and raises every skin in it to attack the enemies trapped inside. The system calls it her second atrocity.

recap.title: War Crime
recap.text: If the war mages hold the castle for six hours, they win. Carl finds their generator and drops an entire inventory folder of explosives on it, labelled Shit Just Hit. The generator goes, and so does every window in the area. Lucia Mar comes up the Nest's stairs after Donut and Mongo, killing Bomo and Toyotomi on the way, and nets Donut in the tower. Donut rolls barrels down at her like Donkey Kong. Raul fights her, Rend saves Mongo by killing Lucia's dog Gustavo, and Carl pours a conscription potion Li Na stole into her. Carl puts on his ring to finish her, and a different voice answers, a child's, who says her name is Diah. There are a hundred and twenty thousand children inside Lucia, and killing her kills the children on Earth's surface. The admins pull her out. Agatha walks off her post. Rosetta, Milk and the tortoise Edgar give Donut a tattoo of a dog on her flank, and it carries a spell from a god in Nekhebit's court. Carl reads the long description of her War Crime spell: two hundred mercenaries paralysed and burning for two weeks. He agrees anyway. From the top of the collapsing Nest, trapped by Lucia's second net, Donut casts it. A spectral paw the size of a district hangs over the ball of enemies, and she swipes down. Three baps, then again, until the screaming stops. The third atrocity makes her the Oak Fell and Champion of Nekhebit. At level one hundred and thirty-five she is the most powerful crawler in the history of the game. Li Na, who marked everyone in the ball, maxes out every stat she has.

recap.title: The long way round
recap.text: Akuma takes the war mages off the floor, and with them whatever they came for, something called the Scavenger's Daughter. On his way out he warns everyone that Agatha is an enemy to them all. The rescue team gets Louis out of the Reaver castle: Juice Box possesses him and teleports him out, leaving a pile of bombs, and the castle goes up with the dragon and the Reaver warlord hidden inside it. The Reavers were rebuilding Louis from the inside, and Epitome Tagg of the Dream is now his heart. The prime minister tries to have Carl ejected, and the AI stops him and threatens his children. Kiwi gives birth to Mongo's twins. Then Samantha admits she was involved in Geyrun's death, and Emberus comes for her, promising to burn the floor in sixty-six minutes either way. Everything happens at once. Katia eats the orchid. Mordecai and Edgar cut Louis open, pull Tagg's machinery out and give him naiad organs from Samantha's golem, and with Tagg dead the Dream is finished. Carl holds the Ring of Divine Suffering up to Donut, and she swallows it. The Sledge casts Zerzura, and all of Larracos, NPCs and all, goes to the twelfth floor, while the surviving former crawlers are put out of the dungeon. The Princess Posse wins Faction Wars. Donut's Laundry Day tears Huanxin Jinx out of Eileithyia, and a plain bolt tipped with Mordecai's mother's ashes kills her. Katia chooses to be made pregnant, which sends her to the surface, where there are children alone who need her. Juice Box goes into the Nothing to be reborn as a weapon. Justice Light springs his trap and breaks it open. Scolopendra wakes. And on the way down, Quasar mentions that Donut's new lawyer is Carl's wife.

floors.previously: On the eighth floor: your planet with the sound off and a card game on top. Carl found out he had a brother, Asher, minutes before the boy's mother put his father down with morphine. Donut learned what happened to Carl's mother. They killed Astrid for a flower that might save Katia, hired an entire strip club, and lost Paz and Anton to a god. Shi Maria is tattooed on Carl's chest. Then a demon prince lifted everyone through the floor, the viewers voted the sponsors' safety off, and here you are. Welcome to Faction Wars.

steps.text: This floor is a war. There are ten teams: nine attacking armies spread around the city of Larracos like slices of a pie, and the city's own NPCs, Team Retribution, defending it. The goal is the castle in the centre. The clock reads thirty days, or ninety hours after a winner is declared. A sixty-hour ceasefire comes first, and while it lasts saferoom rules cover the whole city: attack anyone alive inside the limits and the AI freezes you. When it ends, everyone but Team Retribution and its allies is thrown out of Larracos, though not out of the Shanty Town ring. A crawler who has joined no army by then can be conscripted into one. The protections that kept crawlers regenerating are gone. An attacking team needs to hold the throne room for six hours to win, and a team is out if its warlords die or its own throne room is held for six. There are 293 stairwell chambers, and they stay shut until the war is won or thirty hours remain.

The war runs in four phases: the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos. The Ramp-Up begins when the ceasefire ends and lasts 180 hours. During it there is no offensive magic, no teleporting and no celestial summoning, and nobody but a scout may cross into enemy land except through a kilometre-wide corridor at a fixed place on each border. Once an enemy is through, they move freely. Traps still work if they stay put. Open Hostilities follows when the Ramp-Up expires. The city stays closed to the attackers until only four teams remain; then the Peeling begins, and whoever holds the throne room holds the city's defences. Anything said in a flag room stays hidden from the viewers for eight days.

The ceasefire is over and the Ramp-Up has begun, with 180 hours on its clock. The battle rules hang over every warlord's screen: no offensive magic, no teleport magic or skills, and enemy territory only through a designated corridor, free passage once inside, scouts excepted. Every team's throne is locked in place now, and all the throne rooms show on the map. Nine teams remain; one is already out, its throne room destroyed during the ceasefire.

Half the field is gone. A beaten team's territory passes to the team that beat it, so the map is fewer, larger colours now. Open Hostilities is two hours away, and when the Ramp-Up expires the borders stop meaning anything: an enemy can come from anywhere, and the bans on teleporting and offensive magic lift. Only individual teams, never alliances, may take a throne. Larracos itself is still shut to every attacker until four teams remain.

Four teams remain, and the Peeling of Larracos has begun. The city is open, and the first team to take the castle wins. Alliances count for nothing now: only one team can win. A team that takes the throne room controls the city defence system after a half-hour grace, and it has to hold for six hours. And by an emergency action item granted on the spot, every soldier and warlord of a team that is defeated in this phase drops dead where they stand.

The Princess Posse has won Faction Wars. A winner means the stairwells, and the clock for the floor's destruction is running. The Sledge casts Zerzura, and the whole funnel city of Larracos, Shanty Town with it, is carried to the twelfth floor, its NPCs aboard. The thousands of mercenaries and former crawlers still in the city do not go with it; they are put out of the dungeon the moment the spell triggers. The crawlers who are left take the stairs.

The crawlers come down all over Larracos, City of Dreams. Carl and Donut land face-first in the mud of a wet, stinking alley between two crumbling stone buildings, under a crystal-clear blue sky. The mud smells of the ocean. This part of the city was flooded until very recently; a dead concierge shark lies curled in the corner, suffocated when the drain was opened. It is one of the lowest levels of a funnel-shaped city. Beyond the city are the plains of Larracos, and beyond the plains, woods.

Larracos is a hole in the ground, its top lip three or four hundred feet above the college, and every level of it is a wide ring around an open pit that narrows downward into smoke. The dwarves number the rings from the bottom: sixty-six, they say, though not every ring goes all the way round. Ramps lead from one level down to the next, every other one rigged with explosives. Level fifty holds the College of Magic, a forest of coloured towers growing out of the side of the ring; forty-nine is homes, forty-five is clothing shops. The buildings are gothic stone, columns, arches and gargoyles. A single waterfall falls across the funnel and steps from ring to ring. The water is down to level three now, just enough to cover the highest tower of the castle at the very bottom. Around the top entrance runs Shanty Town, a whole ring of hovels and markets that sprang up after the flood, with food markets, temples and one hidden entrance to Club Vanquisher. It sits outside the city.

From above the floor is a wagon wheel. Larracos sits at the hub inside the thin ring of Shanty Town, and nine nearly equal slices spread out around it across the Plains of Larracos, which are mostly flat except in the north. Spot one belongs to the Bone Clan of the Skull Empire, the only slice with a castle ready built: the King's Point, on a small rocky mountain with lava around it. Their land has the most rivers and lakes, and the biggest river curves through spot two, the rolling hills of the Operatic Collective, then crosses Shanty Town and plunges into the funnel. Spot three is the Princess Posse's: flat, a few hills, and a small lake by the base that seems to be the only real water in the region. Their stronghold, the FUPA, is going up on a hill around a wooden bait-shop saferoom, with palisades, watchtowers and trenches. Spot four, on the far side, is the nagas'. Out past the plains are woods.

The wheel has fewer colours. The Bone Clan hold spots one and two, the Princess Posse three and four, the Dream five and six, the Madness seven and eight, the Reavers nine. The Posse's northern line runs along the region's only river, the border with the orcs, whose castle sits in the only mountains on the battlefield. The old naga land is miles of gently rolling hills, sown with traps. The third front is the round border of Shanty Town, where the Nest is going up: a granite tower built as close to the edge of Larracos as it can stand, by far the tallest thing outside the funnel, tall enough to see the whole battlefield from the top.

Larracos is under siege, the City of Broken Dreams. Smoke fills the funnel and fires burn on every ring. The waterfall has stopped, because the mountain of the King's Point has erupted and a river of lava is crawling toward the lip in its place. On the towers of the college and across the city, jewels glow on top of tall pillars: the city's defence towers, counting down to fire. The castle at the bottom is still under water. Up on the edge, the Nest hangs over the whole funnel, glowing in the dark. Out on the plains the Dream castle has collapsed.

Larracos is gone. Where the city stood there is only a massive pit, its slope bare but for a few saferoom doors, one of them at the very bottom. Where the castle was is a bed of roots as thick as elephant trunks, old, dead roots turning to mulch at a touch, lying over a hole that may go all the way down. Shanty Town has gone with the city. Stairwells to the tenth floor stand in the pit, and the battlefield around it is empty.

The map is full of blue dots, crawlers arriving by the hundred, and white dots for the NPCs, every one of them with a slash through it. Those are Team Retribution, the defenders, headquartered in Larracos with no slice of their own. Their warlord is Ferdinand. Purple dots would be enemy combatants. Eight of the nine attacking teams have already signed a truce among themselves, called it the Bloc, and declared war on Team Retribution and on the Princess Posse, the crawlers' own army, whose warlords are Carl and Donut. The Posse has a truce with the NPCs. Each army has recruiters in the city, and a volunteer is treated far better than a conscript.

The NPCs of Larracos are awake. Juice Box opened their eyes, and most of them know about the previous seasons and their past lives, though some cannot understand it. They believe that a dead NPC stays dead, unlike the outworlders, and they are getting ready: on the balconies of the rings dwarves teach boys to stab and bugbears mend chainmail. A few, their memories quickened, remember dozens of seasons. The other armies are outworlders, real people from outside the dungeon. The Madness is led by a Viceroy called Architect Houston, who tortured a dwarf caught sabotaging his fortifications.

Each warlord has an adjutant; the Posse's is Baroness Victory, an orc and a judge. The enemy is the Bone Clan's orcs, the Operatic Collective, the nagas of the Blood Sultanate, the Prism Kingdom, the Dream, the Madness, the Reavers and the Lemig Sortion, and most of their soldiers are mercenaries: security forces from outside, allowed in by a rule change, with pulse rifles and power armour and very few real battles behind them. A hundred thousand of them are massing on the Posse's northern border. The Posse's own soldiers are tens of thousands of former crawlers come down to fight, fortification engineers among them, and the crawlers they recruited.

Three more teams are out: the Prism Kingdom, the Operatic Collective and the Blood Sultanate. What is left is two sides. The Good Guys Alliance is the Princess Posse and Team Retribution; the Bloc is down to the Madness and the Reavers; the Bone Clan and the Dream stand alone. Juice Box has started lending troops, Semeru dwarves and ordinary citizens of Larracos, to hold Shanty Town alongside Li Na's urban defence battalion, a ring of them around the lip of the city.

Five teams are left: the Princess Posse, the Reavers, the Dream, whose castle is now held by Team Retribution, Team Retribution itself, whose castle is held by the war mages, and the War Mage Rebellion. The war mages are a team at last, under a warlord named Agatha, and they can breathe underwater. Gods walk the field, the goddess of chaos and the god of silence among them. In the burning city the NPCs hold what ground they can.

The war is over, and its people are leaving. The NPCs of Larracos and Shanty Town go to the twelfth floor with their city, and the children go with them. The mercenaries, thousands upon thousands, and the former crawlers, about twenty-eight thousand of the fifty thousand who came, are put out of the dungeon. What is left on the floor is crawlers, filing into the stairwells.

Nobody regenerates any more, so a crawler can simply die. For sixty hours the city is safe, and then any crawler outside an army is fair game: every team is good at hunting down strays in the woods beyond the plains, and they can compel a crawler to fight for them as a conscript. The playing field has been made much bigger, and new mobs have been seeded in the outer reaches of the forests.

The mobs at the edge of the map come as a rolling ball of wailing monsters, slower than such a ball should be but still fast, crushing a path through the forest like a screaming bulldozer, and when it breaks apart dozens of armed mobs rain down. On the borders a hundred thousand soldiers are waiting for the ceasefire to end, with weapons and armour from outside the dungeon, and the Dream's long-range artillery is setting up behind them.

The Ramp-Up is trench war. Artillery pounds the lines and the base, the big batteries able to hit anywhere in the territory. Without offensive magic it comes down to traps, rifles and hand to hand, and an enemy mage spamming Fill Hole from afar suffocates soldiers in their own trenches. Everything that comes across comes through the kilometre-wide corridor, and once it is through it can go anywhere.

Open Hostilities means everything at once. Battalions teleport in beside a castle, flaming artillery balls far bigger than before arc over the field, and long-range death rays crackle up from the enemy lines. Gods are loose: two came out of the Gate of the Feral Gods, and the goddess of chaos has been summoned. A demon eviction has begun. The mountain of the King's Point is erupting, and its lava is running into the riverbed that feeds the city.

In the Peeling, Larracos turns on whoever is not holding it. The city defence towers wake for the war mages: each is an automatic tower with a jewel on its pillar, and the red ones fire a level-five Fire Lance ten times a second. Zarogoths, tall, fat, obsidian mobs with claws and a short-range ray, are generated in the city and press up every ring. The river of lava is about to fall over the edge. And any team defeated now loses every soldier on the battlefield in the same instant.

The last danger is a god's deadline. Emberus wants the one who claims a part in his son's death, and if she is not in his presence in sixty-six minutes, he will destroy this world in fire and lava and wrath. The clock on the floor's destruction now reads sixty-six minutes.
