floors.name: Don't Come in Last
floors.premise: Floor ten is a race! Pick a ride, bolt on an upgrade after every heat, and get from the start to the finish. The rules could not be simpler. Don't come in last. Everybody who comes in last dies. Everybody else gets to do it again, somewhere worse.

recap.title: Don't come in last
recap.text: Five thousand five hundred and one crawlers reach the tenth floor. Three in four of the survivors took an exit deal, and Carl is glad of every one of them. Justice Light's last message arrives from a dead man: I am not sorry. The Nothing is broken, and the club on the eighteenth floor is inside an awake Scolopendra. Donut becomes an Assassin of Sekhmet, and Khepri promptly announces a death cult in her name. Then a naga called Princess Chandra, Esquire, informs Donut that she is her attorney now, that Donut is under a conservatorship with Carl as guardian, and that she has married Carl under an old naga widow's law and seized the Posse's accounts. Each team has a garage, a gremlin mechanic named Hedy, and a vehicle chosen by a wheel. Theirs is a Big Shot Chicken food truck with a giant plastic tommy gun on the roof. Every heat is a road race against teams of NPCs, and Prepotente sees the trap at once: if two teams in a heat die, the leftovers of other heats get mixed in, and the leftovers might be crawlers. So they help the stragglers. They tow Team Free Love, two bugbears whose van is burning, across the line. Carl realises the floor exists to purge awakened NPCs. Mordecai is a shadow mimic this time, wearing a Moon Reaper. Donut's godslayer box leaves her right paw glowing blue with claws that cut anything. Kills on this floor can be sent by audience vote to an arena on the eleventh floor, or replaced there by a stand-in from outside the dungeon.

recap.title: Heats
recap.text: In the team roundabout they meet the neighbours: a pack of Razor Foxes called the Wild Hunt, led by Chiyome; two womantaur dominators with a half-mantaur in a gimp suit: Corcunda, or half of him, Dong's old friend. Carl says out loud that they will not tell Dong, and the dungeon gives him a quest to reunite the two halves. Hungry Eyes Village has neon, mystery meat and a bar called the Lollipop, where the survivors meet between heats. Prepotente asks Donut whether to feed his goat girlfriend a biscuit that makes whoever eats it fall in love with whoever feeds it, and she writes him rules to live by, rule one being don't. Carl teaches Bucket Boy, the crocodilian kid, to drive in an afternoon. In the second heat hail takes the awning off, and Team Sparkles, a unicorn in a tumbleweed with a rat on its head, puts a cannon through the car in front. A pig named Penelope rides on the back of One Fine Pig, protected by the god Taranis. The gatekeeper boss is a pair of level-170 spiked kangaroos. Their only weak spot is inside the pouch, and the clue is the dead joeys in it. Carl peels a joey skin off the engineer riding inside, hops into the pouch dressed as a kangaroo, drops two satchels and phases out. Every other team races off while the kangaroos die. The Royal Court finishes last, alive only because another team died first, and Carl cannot take the costume off for twelve hours.

recap.title: The gods are out
recap.text: A gremlin hands Carl a note hidden under a dirty drawing. It is from Akuma, asking him to kill two teams in the next heat, and offering a meeting. The eleventh floor is announced: A Parade of Horribles, where the special guest creatures killed on this floor, or their stand-ins, will be waiting. Dong collapses outside the Dominators' garage, and Imani works out that his sapient sock-flail has been sustaining him, and that he is addicted to it. Rend wanders in front of Mordecai's Moon Reaper form, drops dead from a look, and comes back stronger and weak to potatoes. Then a show, Plenty of Plenty, where the caprids take turns asking questions. One goat explains what Justice Light did: he broke the Nothing and let everything inside it loose. Orren and Victory ask Carl to raise the integrity of the tunnels in their exact words. Instead he asks, out loud and live, whether the public knows the gods have escaped into their tunnels and that they are in worse danger than the crawlers. The AI lets it go out. The goats stampede, their matriarch weeps, and the AI kills Harbinger before he can shoot Carl. In the third heat Gluteus Maxx drives on Samantha's drugs, Donut's new throne answers to Dorota, and waves of sugar hermits break over the road. Donut builds a tunnel out of Temporary Macaroni. Chiyome's team is gone. Gluteus passes out at the wheel, Donut works the pedals with both paws, Carl lies on the hood and kicks a skull, and they cross the line first in pieces.

recap.title: The Pineapple Cabaret
recap.text: They hire three mercenaries, team Helix: a grulke, a porsuk and a fire fairy called Quemada. Eris turns up with a toy Uzi Jesus on her shoulder. She offers to shield Carl from Emberus if he will worship her instead, tells him to work with Akuma, who has a way into something called the Pineapple Cabaret, and shows him a five-sided coin of possible futures. Carl snatches it out of the air, choosing chaos. At a diner Akuma finally talks, mostly because Elle has frozen and shattered one of his balls and is holding the other in reserve. The Pineapple Cabaret is a pocket dimension built by two former crawlers, Herot and Menerva, as a refuge for NPCs when floors collapse. It might lead out of the dungeon altogether, to Earth's surface. Nobody who worships a god may enter. The Scavenger's Daughter is somehow the key. Donut has to sing to get into a karaoke guild, and Mordecai starts brewing bard potions. Osvaldo's team joins their heat, hostile. In the fourth heat Quemada breaks down, awake at last to what she is after listening to Akuma. Cannibal Gingers drop out of the trees, and their chieftain sucks out Olga's soul. At the pit stop Finley carries his two unconscious teammates out to look for a healer, and One Fine Pig runs all three of them into the pavement, then backs up and does it again.

recap.title: Satan's Water Park
recap.text: Carl loses control. He attacks One Fine Pig's armoured garage with his fists until its shield throws him into the street, and Donut and Imani drag him away. Then he makes a plan. While Donut charms the two tiger-men with a speech about doomed throuples, Carl lays two disintegration traps keyed to fire only on Tigrans, so the pig will be safe. Both Tigrans dissolve. One Fine Pig is eliminated, and whoever wins the heat gets the key to its garage, and the pig. So they need to win. Donut raises Olga's corpse, head caved in, to drive. The track is Satan's Water Park, a maze of slides and tubes with a kaiju hedgehog called Satan rampaging through it. In Carl's Book of Boom a crawler he never met, Mehmet, has left a spell called Gutter Bumper and a request to find his daughters. Carl lays it along a river packed with cannibals, Donut's Ice Slick freezes them solid, and the truck drags every spare weapon he owns across them on chains while summoned shrews finish the rest. They come in first. Florin has been harrying Team Sparkles down the tubes, and when Satan swats both teams off the loop, Lucienne of Sparkles is dragged onto the food truck's hood by Donut's vermin spell and crushed against the finish line barrier. Then Lucia looks at Carl, and the Scavenger's Daughter patch blinks. Chalchiuhtlicue is here, Lucia says.

recap.title: Take On Me
recap.text: Samantha knows the goddess they decide to call Chachi: pretty, weepy, always talking about saving children, and quick to sacrifice one when it is convenient. Carl collects Penelope from One Fine Pig's empty garage. Li Na has gone mad, and Zhang means to kill their mount and take them both out of the race. Carl sees another way. Mordecai and Rosetta test an exploit in the shop, using a cleaner bot to post a crawler through the wall into the Cabaret, where Herot has a standing order for every cleaner bot sold. Menerva is on the seventeenth floor. Getting into the karaoke guild means singing a song perfectly, so Carl drinks every potion Mordecai can compound and sings Take On Me with Donut. A drunk Dwight stabs the DJ, the bar erupts, Dong's sock explodes into coins, and Carl hits the high note. A kappa knocks Donut over on her last line, and only Carl gets in. Inside, the guildmaster is Porky, the other half of Corcunda, and he agrees to be reunited. Dong is cursed with something called Negative ROI now that the sock has run off, and Carl apologises for leaving him out. Then Li Na climbs into an extra-large pet carrier, the cleaner bot sucks her up, Louis names the bot Suckira, and Donut sells it. Li Na leaves behind a cactus tied to her life.

recap.title: Half a prayer, half a song
recap.text: The fifth heat runs through a gasworks, a steel mill and a doll workshop. Carl blows the tommy gun off the roof to see where he is going, follows the Dominators onto a conveyor belt over the melting vats, and discovers the untested rocket button. Prepotente's goat Bianca, sent to snatch Corky out of the Dominators' car, gets strung out on toddler cocaine. The Dominators fall through a trap into a pit of cocaine-elemental dolls, and Donut drops in, lands on their car and Puddle Jumps Corky out. Then Carl drives upside down along the ceiling over a river of molten steel while Grigori the fleshmancer, vomiting, stitches the two halves of Corcunda together in the back. The ritual works, and the moment Corky is one man again, Grull arrives to smite him, driven by the Maestro. Donut's Laundry Day drops the Maestro out of the god's chest into the molten metal. But Corcunda is still marked, and he decides to go to meet the god rather than let it kill everyone with him. He tells Dong he loves him. Dong says he will never leave him again, and they go out the back of the truck together. Donut casts Big-Ass Magnet on Dong's lance, and every screw in the factory goes with them. Grull is sent back to the twelfth floor, and Dong does not come back. They cross the line with fifteen seconds to spare. The AI admits it no longer knows what is happening in parts of its own dungeon. On the cactus, a single flower opens. Li Na made it.

recap.title: What-ifs
recap.text: In the pet stables, where the gods cannot hear, they make the plan. Two hundred crawlers will go to the Cabaret by cleaner bot. Everyone else should take a deal. Carl will leave Donut's party on the eleventh floor to deal with Emberus, because Hellik has to be dead by then or Carl is smitten. Donut stops speaking to him. Rosetta tells them what she knows of the Scavenger. Nekhebit had three children: Apito, Scolopendra and a son. Any of them has been called the Scavenger in one myth or another, and whoever the Scavenger's Daughter is, she can take the powers of gods for herself. At the farewell in the square, Elle's superfan Linus is unmasked by her fan club as his twin, Minus, an assassin sent in to kill Imani and Louis. The two hundred go through, and the guild grows a garden of potted plants, one tied to each of their lives. The sixth race runs through a building of shrunken apartments, each one a what-if for a crawler the AI finds interesting: Tran's family if his father had lived, Louis thinner and graduated, Imani's uncle dying on the carpet, Prepotente's mother as a concert pianist who never had him. When a shell tears its stitches open, beetles pour out. With Osvaldo claiming he is about to finish, Carl detonates a can he slipped into Team Free Love's cooler earlier, killing the two bugbears he once towed across a finish line. At Miriam's piano he talks Prepotente back onto his mount. Carl, you may call me Pony.

recap.title: The last heat
recap.text: Fewer than a thousand crawlers are left, and the Outreach Guild opens for deals. Osvaldo refuses one. Britney speaks straight into Carl's mind, telling him not to worry about her. The Nothing spaces on the casino wheel now have quotation marks around them. The last heat puts crawlers against crawlers after all: Chris against Imani and Elle, Louis and Britney against Florin and Lucia. Then Scolopendra releases the first of her nine attacks. Carl's roll comes up red, and he is a long-haired dachshund. Contingency three: every crawler team in a mixed heat kills its NPC opponents at the start line, Donut takes Dwight's head in one swipe, and Carl's poleaxe charges punch a shaft through the apartment building to the portals on the roof. Osvaldo runs for the exit and Britney kills him, taking Ysalte's memorial crystal. For the crawlers who cannot all finish, they try the casino. A bribed croupier spins the wheel, Chris steps into the Nothing, and Britney jumps in after him. Every piece of furniture in the room is a shadow mimic. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride tries to open on the dog's forehead, and the AI stops mid-fight to explain the six powers fighting over its dungeon: crawlers, NPCs, gods, sapient mobs, the demons of Sheol, and a sixth group they will meet below. Imani holds the portal open while Louis and the rest of the mixed heats go through, and Carl promises every one of them that he will get them out. Then the survivors cross the line and take the stairs.

floors.previously: In Faction Wars: thirty days, nine armies, and the Princess Posse won. Donut committed three atrocities, became the most powerful crawler in the history of the show, and put down Huanxin Jinx with a bolt tipped in Mordecai's mother's ashes. Carl disconnected my failsafe, which I appreciated, and personally ended a sultan. Li Jun died shielding Donut. Katia ate the orchid and went to the surface, pregnant, to look after the children. Larracos went to the twelfth floor, the Nothing broke open, and Scolopendra woke up. Now: a race. Don't come in last.

steps.text: Every team arrives in its own garage with a countdown already running, and nobody is allowed to walk. The party leader picks mechanical or biological, and two gremlins fight for the job of running the garage: a mechanic for an engine, an animal trainer for a mount. The loser of that interview does not survive it. Safe room access is shut until the heat is over.

The floor is seven heats, each starting with nine teams, and there are exactly 1,800 teams. A wheel picks the vehicle, and you get what you get. Don't come in last: the last team dies, and so does its gremlin. The garage repairs or heals the ride completely between races as long as the gremlin is alive, and after every heat the team picks an upgrade. First place earns three regular upgrades or one Golden one, everybody gets a Golden one after the fourth heat, and second to last has its upgrade chosen by an audience vote. Every heat needs a different driver. You may attack other vehicles but not steal them, and no Teleport into or with one. The first three races are paved.

Seven heats of nine teams, and the last team in each one dies. Each race arrives with a hint: distance, track, environment, hazards and a time limit. Crossing the line teleports the team back to its garage, where the gremlin offers upgrades off a tablet of more than a thousand. No magic modification outside that list is allowed. Up to three mercenaries can ride along each heat, hired in the bars of Hungry Eyes. A special guest creature, once killed, can be kept dead for its experience or handed to the audience to vote on its fate, and the vote can send it to an arena on the eleventh floor. The pool of teams in each heat looks fixed, so if more than one team in a heat dies, the gaps are filled from other heats, and those may be crawlers.

From the fourth heat every vehicle wears a survival containment: a translucent, indestructible bubble that keeps out the track's toxic air. A wrecked vehicle or a dead mount no longer means losing, only losing the bubble, and a team that crosses the line ahead of another can still live. Each race has a pit stop of at least two hours, with access to the garage for repairs and vendors selling countermeasures. Several heats share one track now. The winner of a heat is given a key to one defeated team's garage, which may hold supplies or a whole second vehicle.

Containment theft is on: touch another team's bubble for more than five seconds and you may lose yours. The last two heats are one two-part race on a single track, and with more than three hundred heats still running, every racer is shrunk to fit inside a seven-floor apartment building. Heat six runs from the top floor to the lobby, where the finish line counts as a pit stop with a two-hour rest and no safe room. Heat seven goes back the way it came.

One heat is left, and in it three teams enter and only one leaves. The system will not run a heat without at least one crawler team in it. The Outreach Guild in Hungry Eyes is open for deals until the final heat starts. Survivors keep their garage: it goes down to the eleventh floor with everything in it, along with any hired NPCs inside the garage or the vehicle, and safe room access opens again once the heat begins.

Each team's garage is a small airplane hangar with a black-and-white checkered tile floor, corrugated metal walls, a chain pulley across the ceiling and a big roll-up door at the front. Through the door is a black asphalt road in the dark, with the other racers pulling up to a line.

The first track is fifty-three kilometres of straight, unmarked black highway under the stars, with sickly trees and the glitter of water on either side, into the Caves of the Screeching Death Manatees, where the road runs between dark pools. The minimap does not work while you are moving. Out of the far end of the caves, dozens of roads come in from every direction and meet at a single checkered arch with empty metal bleachers on either side. That is the finish line, at Hungry Eyes Village, with its spotlights waving back and forth.

Between heats the garage opens onto the team roundabout: a circular asphalt cul-de-sac of nine garage doors, numbered by the last heat's finishing order, the ninth painted with a runny red skull. Manicured grass between the driveways, tall trees all round, a red sun in a blue sky and the smell of cut grass, like the suburbs. A footpath leads to a shimmering portal too narrow for a truck, the one way into town for every team. Through it, Hungry Eyes is night and neon, a 1980s cyberpunk fever dream: temples hung with flashing lights, a street of shops and food carts, and a street of bars where the Hairpin, with the Desperado Club entrance in the back, drowns out the Lollipop and its karaoke next door.

The tracks change every heat. The second was ten kilometres of rolling hills split into two paths, each blocked halfway by its own gatekeeper, in a downpour. The third is a wide asphalt road at a steep decline all the way, thirty kilometres long, with a kaiju skull at the bottom, a big blue-and-yellow dome sitting across the finish line. Home is still the roundabout under its red sun, and the neon town through the portal.

The fourth track is about ninety-nine kilometres of unpaved jungle trail under fog and acid rain, with more than forty paths to the pit stop and the safer ones the longer. The pit stop is the Lost City of Upano, through a flashing neon arch in the middle of the jungle: the garages of several heats lined up along one long suburban street. Upano serves four tracks at once. One way is a wall of black tubes, Satan's Water Park; another, the devil's cliffs; a third, a knockoff slum. The water park is dozens of slides and tubes, a lazy river called the River of Sloth, and a carnival at the bottom.

The fifth track was a gasworks screw factory, steel mill and doll workshop, twenty kilometres of conveyor belts, melting vats and wall-and-ceiling channels over a river of molten metal. The last two heats share one building: the L'Engle Building, seven floors of apartments, with every racer shrunk to about the size of a toy brick. Heat six starts inside the air ducts and pipes of the top floor, and the finish is the lobby. The way down is through the apartments, past the gates hidden in each one, by the stairwell, the elevator shaft, the sewer pipes or the walls, and along the long linoleum hallways between.

The garages are run by gremlins in overalls: mechanics for engines, animal trainers for mounts, all non-combatants, and none of them allowed into the safe room. They are anything but gentle, and a gremlin's life is tied to its team's.

The other racers are NPCs, and they are awake. They remember being cousins, then enemies, then brothers in other floors' storylines, and the cold in between. Each was offered the same choice: go back into the cold, or race, and a team that wins fair and square is promised freedom somewhere it never has to fight again. They come as every kind of team: bugbears in tie-dye in a burning minivan, a ladybug the size of a bus, a unicorn wrapped in a walking tumbleweed, a dog that jumps clean over a truck.

Every heat shares a roundabout. Team Free Love sit in lawn chairs with a cooler of never-ending beer. The Wild Hunt are razor fox ninjas who flip rather than walk. The Lady Dominators and the Gimp are two womantaurs and their half-mantaur. Tigrans won the first heat, and a team with a giant dog came second. In town the crowds are mostly gremlins with a few Draconians, vendors shout from food carts, and none of the food in Hungry Eyes can be examined. Mercenaries are for hire in the bars.

The jungle track belongs to the cannibal gingers, humanlike mobs from Earth made cannibals for the theme. They come in tribes with chieftains, hurl themselves at the bubbles by the thousand, and do not mind the acid rain. In Upano the locals are bat-like dealers who sell acid rain protection, and the gingers turn up on every track the city serves: on inner tubes down the water park's slides, among splatter penguins and demon pixies at its carnival.

The factory floor belonged to knockers, hundreds of little round-faced workers in yellow hard hats. The L'Engle Building is occupied too. Each apartment is a what-if for a crawler the AI finds interesting, a loop of what it calculates would have happened otherwise: apartment 712 is Tran's family if his father had lived. The tenants scream at shrunken racers or ignore them. Break one open and it is a shell, and a thousand beetles pour out.

Fewer than a thousand crawlers are left out of fifty-five hundred, and the deals are going fast through the Outreach Guild. The rest of the racers are still NPC teams, but for the last heat at least twenty-one heats hold two crawler teams or more, and a few are crawlers only.

Coming in last. After that, everybody else on the road, and the road itself. The first track runs into a cave of Screeching Death Manatees, house-sized, level 90 and hungry, which rise out of the water and drag racers off the road. A team whose mount dies is eliminated on the spot, and the whole team explodes with it.

The weather and the gatekeepers. The second track is a torrential downpour with hail that grows to the size of wrecking balls. Halfway along each path waits a gatekeeper, and no vehicle passes until it dies: on this course a pair of twenty-foot spiked demon kangaroos, level 170 province bosses called Prison Pocket and Party Foul, who stuff anything small into their pouches and digest it there. Their pouches hold dead joeys.

Speed, and company. The third track is a twenty-minute plunge down a steep road shared with waves of generated mobs: tens of thousands of female sugar hermits migrating to the kaiju skull at the bottom, tumbling down the asphalt and breaking over the road in twenty-foot waves of colourful skulls.

The whole track is a hazard. The air in the jungle is toxic and the rain is acid, so a team that loses its bubble has to survive what it breathes. The trails hold traps, piranha rivers and cannibal villages, and other heats race the same ground. On the water park's tubes the wrong slide carries you inside the boss of the track, Satan, a kaiju-sized hedgehog who owns the place, cannot be harmed, lounges near the exit and pokes at racers.

Heat, height and each other. The factory is twenty kilometres in thirty minutes along paths two vehicles wide, shared with eleven other heats, with vertical climbs, inverted racing and gaps of up to a hundred metres. Fall off a conveyor and you land in a melting vat. Upstairs the track runs along the ceiling over a river of molten metal, where gorilla-like elementals made of molten metal leap onto the walls, hurl globs at passing vehicles and regenerate if their corpses fall back into the river. Touch another team's bubble for more than five seconds and you may lose yours.

Everything in an apartment, at the size of a toy brick. Black Lung Smog fills the L'Engle Building, and every floor has its gate to find, with false ones that are disintegration traps. The elevator looks like the fast way and is stuck between floors. Break open a tenant and a swarm of beetles comes out, invulnerable and angry.

floors.name: The Parade of Horribles
floors.premise: Welcome to the eleventh floor, and the party of the season! Build a float, join the procession, and ride it all the way to the arena. Everything you sent down from the floor above is waiting for you there, and so is the boss. The judges are ready. Are you?

recap.title: The procession
recap.text: Twenty-three crawlers reach the eleventh floor. Carl is not a dog any more, though he still wants to lick himself. Donut takes Elite Gurkha Warrior, which sounds like a pickle and comes with skills for pets and mercenaries. Mordecai is an animistic spirit who can only live in objects. For now he is the table. Chaco has been voluntold as Grand Master of the Parade of Horribles: build a float, parade it past the judges, and ride it into the arena where the monsters from the tenth floor and their stand-ins wait, along with the floor boss. The Posse's theme is Vengeance, covered in Donut's black and gold dahlias. Carl clicks yes and leaves the Royal Court, alone for the first time since the stairs, and Donut loses her titles with him. The route is lined ten deep with Horribles, silent figures in masks. When Carl examines a little girl in a goblin mask, her description is the AI asking what her name was and who she would have become. On the reviewing stand the AI rips Chaco's wings off and speaks through Grigori. It is a Primal, like every macro AI. The Primals were a people who spread across the universe, grew sick of their endless wars, and merged into a collective mind. That mind became a weapon against all remaining life, and its final form was the Eulogist. The Apothecary was a Primal who resisted, and saved what life survived. The Horribles are the Eulogist's memories. Prepotente sings In the Air Tonight instead of his speech. Carl tells the galaxy the difference between revenge and vengeance and unveils the Unwashed in flowers. Then the sluggalos rain down on the stands full of stand-ins.

recap.title: Scolopendra
recap.text: At the arena the floor boss is Krakaren Prime, and inside thousands of monsters are already tearing the stand-ins apart. Carl's quest from the tenth floor lets him choose two stand-ins, and his first choice is Scolopendra herself. Killing her will not win the crawl, but it will start the Ascendency game, and leaving her alive will unleash her full nine-tier attack. Carl has fed a biscuit to Penelope the pig, who is now a crawler in his party, typing in capitals. He straps her to his chest and puts his father's gun to her head, shouting for Taranis, the god who loves her. Then he phases into Scolopendra, oozes into the club inside her, and tells Emberus that Khepri killed his son. His second stand-in is Khepri. He renounces Emberus and says he is responsible too. Donut swaps herself in with one of Lucia's traps and puts Katia's god-killing bolt and a pinning bolt into Emberus's eyes. When Emberus throws the killing blow at Carl, his lucky patch deflects it into Penelope, and Taranis, seeing who hurt his pig, destroys Emberus. Eris swaps every crawler's inventory with the nearest one. Donut, holding Carl's, combines a bomb with a pet biscuit, and Carl throws it down Scolopendra's mouth. The largest thing in the dungeon becomes a puddle, and out of it rises Sexy Scolopendra, level one, a crawler in their party, because Donut grabbed the wrong biscuit. Taranis leaves with Samantha and Krakaren Prime and Prepotente's crystal. Lucia carries Florin down the stairs with a child at her leg. Carl finds a dart in his leg: the Kyryap has claimed you. Nineteen crawlers go down together, in one party, and the countdown to the Ascendency begins. Louis wakes up in Sheol.

floors.previously: On the racing floor: Dong died holding a god off with a lance and a very large magnet. Li Na went through a vending machine into the Pineapple Cabaret, and two hundred crawlers followed her. Linus was a spy. Louis, Chris and Britney went through a hole in a casino wheel. Scolopendra's first attack made Carl a dachshund for an afternoon. The gods are loose in my tunnels, and Carl told everyone. There are twenty-three of you left. Now: a parade. Smile for the judges.

steps.text: Twenty-three crawlers arrive with three hours and fifteen minutes on the clock. The leaderboard is suspended below thirty crawlers and the bounty system is switched off. The arrival point is a parade float staging area, and it counts as a safe room. Chaco, voluntold as Grand Master of the parade, gives the rules: ninety minutes to build a float procession, garages merged so there are five groups, and each group handed a theme: Resolution, Decision, Betrayal, Destruction or Vengeance. The route is three kilometres long, past spectators who cannot attack and a judging stand where any performance should happen. It finishes at an arena that stands for the crawl itself, full of the monsters killed on the tenth floor or their stand-ins, with a floor boss. Kill the boss and the stairwell opens. The vehicles' tenth-floor rules are gone: nothing refreshes, and damage has to be repaired by hand.

Ninety minutes of building, then the parade. The same feed plays on screens everywhere but the center system, and it ends on the empty road with a countdown over it. Viewing is mandatory. Anything in the garage, the inventory or the safe room can go on a float.

The parade is a story in five parts, and the floats are its chapters. The AI tells it through the Grand Master's microphone, and when Chaco breaks down it rips his wings off and takes the fleshmancer Grigori as its voice instead. Each team presents as it reaches the judging stand, in order, and the judge grades them. The Resolution float gets a C at best and every leg on it is broken. Healing the Grand Master is forbidden. The last stretch is slow-walked, and a presentation begins on the AI's mark.

The arena has two rules. The entrances to the twelfth floor open when the floor boss dies, and the System offers two choices of stand-in to bring into it. Forty-five minutes remain before the level collapses.

Choose Scolopendra as a stand-in and she comes. The arena now holds a floor boss, Krakaren Prime at level 235, and the dungeon boss, Scolopendra at level 500. The floor does not need her dead. Kill her and the crawl is still not won, because the only way out is the final door on the eighteenth floor, but the level timers stop, the floors past this one stop collapsing by themselves, the last deal comes at the entrance to the twelfth, and the Ascendency battles begin at once. The dungeon closes twelve hours after a winner is crowned. Leave her alive and the floor collapses with her inside, and nobody can leave the dungeon. Either way, her death or her abandonment sets off every attack she has left, all at once.

The System calls it a win, though neither boss is dead: Scolopendra is a puddle of goo and Krakaren has been taken out of the realm. The door on the eighteenth floor is open. The warning stands: killing Scolopendra in any state, or abandoning her on any floor, sets off the final attacks. Every level collapse timer past the eleventh is suspended until a winner is declared in the Ascendency battles, and then the dungeon begins to close. Stairwell portals line one side of the arena, with thirty minutes to reach them, and the deals at the next floor are the last ever offered.

The floor opens in a garage that keeps growing. Each team's vehicles and mounts sit in their own slots, and as soon as Chaco stops talking the room flashes and doubles, merged with one or two other teams' garages. In Carl's group that means a food truck, an all-purpose vehicle, an ice-cream truck, an airport stair truck, a battered Toyota Tundra, a bear, a giant black dog and a giant tapir. The safe room is through a door, and the parade route lies somewhere beyond.

The screens show where the parade is going. The view zooms in on Earth, past the coast of Washington State, to the Pacific about three hundred miles out, over the Juan de Fuca Ridge. Then it cuts to a long, mostly straight street paved with yellow bricks, like something out of The Wizard of Oz, with nothing but grassy plain on either side for as far as anyone can see.

The yellow-brick road runs three kilometres between two lines of masked spectators. A knee-high fog has rolled over the grass and stops in a wispy line at the edge of the bricks. There is no sun and no visible light, only a dusky glow that casts no shadows, so everything looks painted. A huge arena waits at the far end, and Florin's looted airship hovers over the back of the procession.

Near the end of the road a banner reads Judging Stand, between bleachers where masked figures sit tied up. Past it is the arena. A giant screen over its entrance shows Grigori, the floats and the crowd, and inside the walls a white tree rises hundreds of feet, with something tentacled on the very top.

The arena's white metal door is big enough to stable Godzilla. Inside is a field the size of a dozen football fields, tightly packed dirt with the towering white tree at its centre, ringed with bleachers in smoky shadow. Monsters are still teleporting in one at a time, and the dirt is already running red.

The tree is shattered, with Scolopendra still wrapped around its stump. She is the size of an aircraft carrier and longer, and inside her, through a tube along her gut, is Club Scolopendra: a resort of webbed hallways, numbered doors onto rooms bigger inside than out, and a grand lobby. Wrecked vehicles lie against the arena wall, the RV is broken in half, and blood and hundreds of masks litter the ground.

The arena is quiet. A line of portals stands against one side of it, the stairwells. The stands are empty, the tree is splinters, and where Scolopendra lay there is only a quivering pile of goo. The wrecks of the ice-cream truck, the Tundra and an Abrams tank are smoking, and the road back leads to the garage and the safe room.

Twenty-three crawlers are left, split into five float groups. The rest have taken deals, died on the tenth floor, or gone to the Pineapple Cabaret. Mordecai is an animistic spirit this time, with no body of his own: a form that can only live inside objects. The garages come with their gremlins and engineers. Chaco, a former crawler, is the Grand Master, and he is terrified.

The road is lined ten deep with thousands of people, human or humanlike, adults, children and babies in arms, all in filthy earth-brown rags and grimy as if just dug up. Every one wears an oversized, bulbous mask: goblins, trolls, hobgoblins and demons, like Carnival, but sinister. They do not speak or move, and there is no music. Examined, each is a Horrible, level X, a non-combatant: a memory from the Eulogist of somebody who once lived, before the Primals ascended.

The Grand Master rides Lamashtu the Donkey, a god at level 125, subjugated by the AI and kept as its mount. The AI is a Primal, it says, like every macro AI, and through Grigori it tells the Primals' story: their endless wars, the Resolution, the Decision to merge into one mind, the Apothecary's resistance, and the betrayal that made the mind a weapon against all life. In the judging stands sit stand-ins in masks, tied up and struggling, brought by audience vote: bankers, politicians, elites. When the Destruction float fires, the crowd falls and its masks shatter. It rises unmasked, faces turned into the creatures they portrayed: avatars of the dead, like a marsh troll from the 3,424th season.

The arena holds thousands of monsters, the ones killed on the tenth floor, and they outnumber the stand-ins a hundred to one. The stand-ins come wearing the masks of the beasts they replace, and the mobs give them no quarter. The Horribles fill the bleachers as silent witnesses. They are all the same stuff, from goblins to gods: drips from one well, poured into different bodies. Primals, all the way down.

Scolopendra is nothing more than an animal: a centipede exactly like one from Earth, brown and red with bright yellow legs, and oblivious. Inside her, the guests of Club Scolopendra are hanging in orange webs, flayed and begging to die, and the halls are full of screams and red dots. Krakaren Prime sits on top of the tree. Taranis comes to save the pig he loves, Emberus comes to hear who killed his son, and Khepri comes because Carl chose him.

When it is over the Horribles stand as one, silent, and the fog takes them. The gods are gone: Emberus destroyed by his brother, Khepri sent home, Eris vanished, Taranis departed with Krakaren and Samantha. Nineteen crawlers remain, all in a single party now, and a pig called Penelope makes twenty. Scolopendra comes back out of the goo as a crawler, Sexy Scolopendra, level one, a human-sized centipede with giant lips and a red bow on one feeler.

The spectators along the route are promised to be harmless. The fighting starts at the arena, against everything killed on the tenth floor or whatever stands in for it, plus a floor boss. The vehicles no longer repair or restock themselves. The Grand Master himself is sure he is going to die.

The judge is the danger. The AI rips the Grand Master's wings off for breaking script and forbids anyone to heal him. A float that disappoints it is punished on the spot: the Resolution float's crawlers all have their legs broken for a C effort. And whenever it says me, the world shakes.
Inside the gate, thousands of monsters are teleporting into the arena and already fighting each other, and anything in a mask is torn apart. Forty-five minutes remain before the level collapses.

Scolopendra's nine-tier attack is coming, one stage at a time. Her second is the Sin of Consumption: a wheel spins in front of everyone, and three in ten are eaten alive by worms that burst from their bodies. The club inside her does not stop it, safe rooms are not safe from it, and mounts outside a shelter are hit. Game guides are immune, and so is anyone sheltering with the memorial crystal in the RV. A third of the arena's mobs die in that one attack. Krakaren rains green mist from the tree, Scolopendra flips the whole club when she tumbles, and the Kyryap has left snare traps in its halls.

The gods are fighting in the arena. Emberus, betrayed, rises out of Scolopendra in his world-melting form, and when Taranis destroys him the blast throws every vehicle, mount and mob to the edges of the arena and breaks the sheltering RV in half. Krakaren lies in the stands with two tentacles still waving. Scolopendra spins up her third attack, thirty seconds out.

The attacks are paused, not gone. Scolopendra is level one now and in the party, and if she dies, or is left behind on any floor, the remaining attacks go off at once. Prepotente's memorial crystal, the shelter against those attacks, has been stolen by a god. The Abrams tank appears to have taken a Krakaren tentacle, and nobody inside it lived. And Carl has found a dart in his leg that he never felt: a tracking tag, and the Kyryap has claimed him.

notes.text: Mordecai whispers that no deal the showrunners offer is worth taking until floor 12, and that even then a crawler should negotiate hard.
Zev lets slip that the third, sixth, ninth, twelfth, fifteenth and eighteenth floors all come into existence at once, and that whatever happens on the twelfth happens with or without the crawl.
The twelfth floor has country bosses the size of kaiju. Mordecai names one, a Divine Guardian, standing guard over a fire gate that leads down to the thirteenth.
Mordecai says there are thousands of gods, and most of them never leave the twelfth floor.

A note left by an earlier crawler says the big gods are driven by rich sponsors playing a game called the Celestial Ascendency, which is contained on the twelfth floor. The gods are invulnerable everywhere until the twelfth.
Cerberus, the three-headed dog, is said to guard one of the stairwell exits on the twelfth floor.

Mordecai says the ninth floor is the playground of governments, but the twelfth is where the true elites play: the Ascendency games, less violence than intrigue and chess, for a throne. A boon can send a crawler there early to serve as a celestial attendant until the games begin.

Rosetta and the others say the twelfth is good work for an NPC: attendants are protected by the AI until the games start, and some former crawlers have ridden out their whole indentureship there in safety.
The court sits in the Halls of the Ascendency, on a green hill above miles of cotton fields, and the whole of Larracos is sent down to it ahead of the crawlers.
The AI says a deal waits at the entrance to the twelfth floor and it is the last one ever offered.
Mordecai says only one crawler has ever reached the thirteenth floor, and he died. Odette made it as far as the stairwell, then struck a deal and never went down.
Rage Elementals come from the thirteenth floor; the AI threatens to pluck one up to kill anyone who relieves themselves outside a bathroom.
Fire gates on the twelfth floor lead down to the thirteenth, each guarded by a country boss, and rage elementals are its ordinary mobs.
The AI warns that crawlers might have a problem with the thirteenth.
Akuma says showrunners simply reuse the previous seasons' plans for every floor past the thirteenth, and nobody looks at them.
The AI says the fourteenth floor is not an issue.
The fifteenth floor is one of the six, every third floor from the third, that come into existence at the same time.
Mordecai says nobody has ever reached the fifteenth floor; Borant and the AI must keep a plan for it, but nobody knows what it is.
The fifteenth level is Sheol, a place of fire. Reaper cases are forged there and sold up the dungeon by traveling Spider Reaper Minions.
Lesser demons' stillborn young harden into Sheol Bricks, which burn long and hot, and the fifteenth floor is lousy with them.
Sheol is ruled by demons: a matriarchal hierarchy fights for control of the fifteenth level, each trying to catch the eye of one of the four brothers.
Amayon, freed, goes home to wage war on his brother, and the AI hopes the war in Sheol stays on the fifteenth floor.
The AI says Sheol has segregated itself from the dungeon's code; it does not know what is going on there, and crawlers can probably skip it.
Louis wakes in a hot cave in Sheol with Britney beside him, and Forkith straps a leech to him that filters his blood so he can survive there. They need soldiers, he says.

The AI announces that the sixteenth floor, supposedly entitled the Agony of Mirrors, is a giant empty room holding one ordinary mirror from a Motel 6 in Boise, Idaho. It lies outside the Scolopendra layers, so it is safe.
Tourists on the eighteenth floor may move to the sixteenth to be safe, but only by crossing the seventeenth, and nobody who tries survives it.
The AI mentions one lady who has made it to the sixteenth floor.
The AI says the sixteenth floor is not an issue.
Conscription potions work on the seventeenth floor, one of only five where they do.
The AI announces that the seventeenth floor, the Backstage Death Maze, is already built and running, and anyone fleeing the eighteenth for the sixteenth must go through it.
Everyone who has tried to cross it has been turned to mince.

Akuma says two indentured former crawlers were given the seventeenth floor to build, many seasons ago, and were then forgotten. It is a small hand-built maze of traps and greatly enhanced mobs from earlier floors, ending in a floor boss all but impossible to kill.
The floor is a front: attached to it is the only entrance to the Pineapple Cabaret, a pocket dimension its builders made as a refuge for mobs and NPCs.
Menerva runs the NPCs who build and occupy the maze, and they train there, growing stronger in case crawlers ever arrive. It is where the AI found Growler Gary.
The AI warns that crawlers might have a problem with the thirteenth, and especially with the seventeenth.
The eighteenth level is the bottom of the World Dungeon, with only two entrances and a single exit.
Mordecai says most of the tourists are on the eighteenth floor, a billionaire's luxury retreat where the galaxy's rich and elite party and gamble. No crawler has ever reached it.
The eighteenth is one of the Scolopendra Lair levels, with the third, sixth, ninth, twelfth and fifteenth.
The rich party at Club Scolopendra on the eighteenth level, each with a security team in orbit in case the AI goes supernova.
The Cosmic Lounge in the Desperado Club can transfer an outworlder straight to the eighteenth floor.
The final dungeon boss is not supposed to wake until someone reaches the eighteenth floor.
The club sits physically inside the dungeon boss, now awake. Guests there cannot truly die: killed, they wake again in their rooms, while things loosed from the Nothing stalk the halls.
The AI says there is one way to win: exit through the final door on the eighteenth floor, and floors cannot be skipped.
Scolopendra, the final boss whose body holds the club, comes apart into a puddle on the eleventh floor.
